item.title: Shama: Around 7,500 Bangladeshis imprisoned in Saudi Arabia
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed has said around 7,500 Bangladeshis are imprisoned in different parts of Saudi Arabia.
She added that the government is checking whether two Bangladeshis sentenced to death are on the list.
“They send us the figures, and these people are in prison for various offences. We are checking whether the names of the two people sentenced to death are on that list. We have not received detailed information yet. We have requested copies of the verdicts from the Saudi government. We will be able to learn more once we receive them,” she said.
The state minister made the remarks on Friday after the body of Bangladeshi worker Md Shahed Ahmed, who was killed in a missile attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, was handed over to his family.
Shama Obaed said every country has its own legal framework under which punishments are imposed. However, Bangladesh needs to be informed when its citizens are sentenced in such cases.
She said the government was pursuing legal avenues to seek clemency for Bangladeshis sentenced in Saudi Arabia and other countries.
The state minister also said the bodies of 11 Bangladeshis killed in conflicts in the Middle East over the past six months had been brought back to the country, while efforts were underway to repatriate the remaining bodies.
Addressing Shahed Ahmed’s family, she said the government would provide financial assistance to them soon.
Regarding Bangladeshis who have been beheaded in Saudi Arabia, she said further details could be provided once the Saudi government supplied copies of the verdicts. She reiterated that the government was pursuing legal avenues to seek clemency for Bangladeshis sentenced in Saudi Arabia and other countries.
She added that the government was also working on issues concerning visa renewals and employment for expatriate Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Cop, BNP leader killed as covered van hits them in Gazipur
item.description:
A local BNP leader and a sub-inspector of Kaliganj police station were killed after a covered van hit them during a night patrol in Kaliganj, Gazipur, early Friday.
Two other police personnel were injured, one of them critically. The driver of the covered van fled the scene.
The accident occurred in front of Kaliganj Government Shramik College in the Tumlia area on the Tongi-Ghorashal regional road around 3:30am on Friday.
Ashraful Islam, officer-in-charge (investigation) of Kaliganj police station, confirmed the incident.
The deceased BNP leader, Rafiqul Islam alias Rafiq Molla, 48, was the organising secretary of Ward 2 of Kaliganj municipality BNP. He was the son of late Waz Uddin of the Tumlia area.
The deceased police officer was Sub-Inspector Mizanur Rahman. The injured police personnel were also posted at Kaliganj police station. Constable Fazle Rabbi, who was driving, was taken to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital in Gazipur.
Additional Superintendent of Police for Kaliganj Circle Sheikh Muttazul Islam said a police team led by SI Mizanur Rahman was on patrol in front of Kaliganj Government Shramik College that night.
The officers had stopped by the roadside and were questioning several suspicious individuals when an unidentified covered van hit them, leaving Mizanur Rahman, Police Sub-Inspector Jabed Omar, Constable Fazle Rabbi and BNP leader Rafiqul Islam seriously injured.
The van driver dragged Mizanur Rahman for nearly half a kilometre before leaving him by the roadside and fleeing towards Ghorashal.
A passerby and a rickshaw puller rescued the injured and took them to Kaliganj Upazila Health Complex.
Mustafa Al Hossain, the on-duty physician at the health complex's emergency department, declared Rafiqul Islam dead at 3:55am.
Mizanur Rahman and Jabed Omar were later referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment. Mizanur was declared dead at 6:47am while undergoing treatment. Jabed remains under treatment at the hospital.
According to locals, police launched an operation around 3am to arrest Ohid Molla, an alleged drug trader from the Madhakhola area. After the arrest, the team was returning to the police station when they reached the college area.
Mizanur and the other officers were talking to local BNP leader Rafiqul Islam Molla, who was standing there, when the speeding covered van struck them.
Kaliganj police station Officer-in-Charge Zakir Hossain said no one had been arrested in connection with the incident, and the driver and vehicle had yet to be identified. Legal proceedings are underway.

item.title: Remains of two Bangladeshis killed in Riyadh airport attack arrive home
item.description:
The mortal remains of one of the two Bangladeshis, who were among 13 people killed in a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, arrived home on Friday morning.
The body of Shahed Ahmed Ashik reached Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka around 8:30am, where State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam received it, according to the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment.
Later, the body was handed over to the victim's family. During the handover, the Wage Earners' Welfare Board provided immediate financial assistance to the victim's family.
The assistance included Tk35,000 to cover burial and transportation costs and a special grant of Tk50,000 following his death in the conflict.
Meanwhile, the victim's employer, Saad Al-Essa Contracting Company, deposited 27,395.62 Saudi Riyals, equivalent to around Tk9 lakh, into the account of the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh.
The amount covers his outstanding salary, allowances and service benefits. It will be formally handed over to his family through the Wage Earners' Welfare Board soon.
The family may also receive an additional Tk3 lakh, subject to having a valid Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) card or equivalent identification.
Besides, the family could be eligible for a further Tk10 lakh in insurance benefits, depending on the applicable insurance coverage, the ministry said.
Thirteen people, including two Bangladeshis, were killed in the attack on King Khalid International Airport on October 10. The attack also left 308 others, including several Bangladeshis, injured.
Shahed, 35, son of Rafiqul Islam alias Mithu of Malipara village in Madla union under Shajahanpur upazila of Bogura, was among the deceased.

item.title: The psychological wall between cultural and national identity
item.description:
It seems the city authority, in trying to do a good thing, has landed in serious trouble. In the middle of it all, there was an unwelcome tug-of-war over the portrait of the late Sanjib Chowdhury. This dramatic chain of events around the wall doesn’t only raise questions about the city authority’s judgement. It also points to a social, political, and psychological problem in Bangladesh.
Among Bangladesh’s many problems is the fact that it has two “ages.” As an independent state, Bangladesh is only 55 years old. But on the basis of the Bengali language and culture, the Bengali nation is very old. Reconciling the two should not be a problem. But religious division, and its influence on society and politics, has made this simple task difficult.
Take the wall of the Shilpakala Academy in Segunbagicha. The Dhaka city authority decided to clear hawkers from the footpath beside the road and decorate the wall beautifully. Good. They decided that, instead of using bright colours alone, they would also paint portraits of some of the country’s eminent figures. Better still.
Trouble broke out over whose portraits. The question arose: What do we mean by “country,” and even if these figures are eminent, are they really “ours?” And what exactly do we mean by “ours?”
The country is only 55 years old, so finding “eminent” figures is also hard. It may sound a little harsh, but it isn’t untrue. In any society, it takes time for a poet, writer, musician, politician, or intellectual to be counted as eminent.
Today there are many people, living or dead, who are enormously popular. But it will take them a long time, a very long time, to reach the eminent or classic level.
From Shakespeare to Nazrul
In the Western world, this matter doesn’t create much controversy. Britain’s The Beatles and America’s Elvis Presley are undoubtedly the most popular modern musicians in the West.
But when portraits are placed on currency or in nationally important places, the West goes back to its classical era, whether in music, literature, or painting. Many people dislike Britain’s former prime minister Winston Churchill. But his huge statue in Parliament Square, for leading Britain in the Second World War, and his picture on the £5 note don’t cause much controversy. (Though far-left youths occasionally smear red paint on the statue, because in their eyes Churchill was a symbol of racist imperialism.)
The vast difference between the two categories, eminent and popular, is not understood by many, or they understand it but pretend not to.
This difference does not disrespect popular figures. Rather, it tells their followers that their time will come too. But before that, we must see whether the work of those who are popular today will still be relevant 100 years from now. Will it still be read in schools and colleges, as the literature of William Shakespeare, Rabindranath Tagore, or Kazi Nazrul Islam is taught today? To cross the boundary of popularity and reach the classical level, a person’s work must survive even a hundred years after their death.
By that measure, Sanjib Chowdhury’s portrait does not belong beside Rabindranath’s or Nazrul’s. But that wall is a fitting place for Begum Rokeya or Jibanananda Das, because they are truly eminent. Yet an injustice has also been done to Sanjib Chowdhury. If there was a case for keeping him on the wall, why was he removed? By putting him up once and then taking him down under criticism, the authority has insulted the memory of the late artist, which perhaps did not occur to them.
The deeper problem of the wall
If the city authority had wished, it could have decorated one or two entire walls with portraits of popular writers, musicians, and actors. Beside Sanjib Chowdhury, portraits of popular but late figures such as Ayub Bachchu, Azam Khan, Humayun Faridi, Al Mahmud, Shamsur Rahman, Farida Yasmin, and Zahir Raihan could have found a place.
But even then, problems would have arisen. There are many popular figures, and a fresh controversy would begin over why those left out were not included.
But this wall has exposed an even deeper problem. 55 years after independence, the debate over the country’s and the nation’s self-identity has still not stopped, as we have once again been made to see plainly.
Art, literature, music, and cinema are all part of a nation’s cultural life. Language and cultural heritage play the main role here, although at different stages of history, religion has had a big influence in building that heritage.
When people in Bangladesh search for the roots of their culture, when they want to remember the names and work of their own eminent figures, national borders will not be able to hold them back.
Bangladesh’s culture did not begin after the birth of the independent state. In search of the country’s luminaries, many names will come up who are Bengali in heart and soul but whose work was completed before independent Bangladesh was born.
To find the eminent figures of Bangladesh’s cultural world, one has to look beyond not only 1971 but the twentieth century. There, which side of the new border someone’s birthplace fell on after the 1947 partition of India should have no place in the debate.
The greatest Bengali BBC list
That 1971 left a huge mark on the hearts of the people of Bangladesh can be seen from a 2004 experience at BBC Bangla.
BBC Bangla’s plan was to make a series of programs on eminent figures through a listener poll. Listeners were asked: In your opinion, who is the greatest Bengali of all time? And not just one name. It was decided to make a list of 20 and produce a radio feature on the life of each eminent person.
The list shows that, at least, BBC Bangla radio listeners did not take the present national borders into account in choosing the “greatest Bengali.” Rising above religious and political divisions, they looked for their own people.
While fixing the broadcast date, an unexpected surprise came up. Counting the days, it turned out that March 26 to April 14 was exactly 20 days. That meant the series on “the greatest Bengali of all time” could begin on Bangladesh’s Independence Day and end on Bengali New Year’s Day, Pohela Boishakh. What could be a more fitting time for this series?
In the list drawn up from the listeners’ votes, first place went to Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and second to Rabindranath Tagore. Then came Kazi Nazrul Islam, A K Fazlul Huq, Subhas Chandra Bose, and Begum Rokeya Sakhawat. After them came Jagadish Chandra Bose, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani, Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Titumir, Lalon Fakir, Satyajit Ray, Amartya Sen, the martyrs of 21 February, Dr Muhammad Shahidullah, Swami Vivekananda, Atisha Dipankar, Ziaur Rahman, and Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy.
This poll was not without controversy. Some Islamist newspapers found a “Brahminical conspiracy” behind it. A far-left editor saw in the publication of the list an attempt to boost the Awami League’s movement against the then BNP government. But one of my colleagues at the BBC was only surprised.
Achala Sharma, then head of the BBC’s Hindi service, who had learned Bengali only to read Sarat Chandra’s books, expressed her surprise to me. “Why didn’t Rabindranath come first?” she asked. I gave her my analysis. “If this poll had been held 40 years ago, Rabindranath would undoubtedly have been chosen as the greatest Bengali. But in these 40 years, Bangladesh was born, and as the architect of the Bengalis’ first independent state, Mujib’s place in the listeners’ minds has moved above Rabindranath’s.”

item.title: Japan to arrange $6.35 billion in private investment in Bangladesh
item.description:
Japan is expected to arrange private-sector investments worth ¥1 trillion, equivalent to around $6.35 billion, in Bangladesh over the next five years, according to a report published by Japan's Nikkei Asia newspaper.
The proposed investment arrangement is expected to be mentioned in a joint statement following a summit between Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, who is scheduled to visit Japan this month, the report said.
The planned investments are expected to cover automobile and other manufacturing industries, as well as the construction of energy facilities, according to Nikkei.
The investment initiative is also expected to involve companies entering the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone, which is being developed by several parties, including Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corporation.
The proposed investment plan could open up new opportunities for Bangladesh to attract Japanese capital, expand industrial production, diversify its manufacturing base and strengthen energy infrastructure.
Japan has long been an important development partner of Bangladesh, with cooperation spanning infrastructure, trade, investment and industrial development.

item.title: Apratim murder: Police submit charge sheet against four
item.description:
Police have submitted a charge sheet against four people, including two teenagers, in the murder case of Ishayat Shahriar, also known as Apratim, 13, son of Comilla University Bangla Department Associate Professor Nahida Begum.
The charge sheet was filed on Tuesday, 31 days after Apratim’s body was recovered. Police said the investigation found preliminary evidence linking all four accused to the murder.
District police media officer and Additional Superintendent of Police Lutfur Rahman confirmed the submission late Thursday night.
Apratim’s father, KM Firoz Shahriar, who filed the case, said the investigation officer called him on Thursday night to inform him that the charge sheet had been submitted.
Expressing his grief over losing his son, Firoz said the family had many dreams centred on Apratim, but those dreams had been shattered. He called for a speedy trial and the maximum punishment for those responsible.
Rajib Ahmed, an inspector (investigation) at Sadar Dakshin Model police station in Cumilla and the case’s second investigation officer, submitted the charge sheet.
The accused are Saiful Islam, also known as Tuhin, 19; Siam, 19; and two teenagers aged 15 and 16.
Police brought charges under Sections 302, 201 and 34 of the Penal Code, 1860. The two teenagers were identified as children in the charge sheet under the Children Act, 2013.
Investigators said Tuhin played the leading role in planning the murder, while evidence indicated Siam’s involvement in the planning. Three of the accused have been accused of directly participating in the killing, while Siam faces allegations of planning and aiding the crime.
Police also said Tuhin and the two teenagers had given confessional statements before the court.
Despite the submission of the charge sheet, Apratim’s family remains concerned about the actual ages of the two teenagers. The family had previously called for DNA tests, if necessary, to determine their ages. The issue had also prompted questions among teachers and students at the university.
The family said it would consult its lawyer and decide on further legal steps after receiving a copy of the charge sheet.
Additional Superintendent of Police Lutfur Rahman said the investigation had been completed and the charge sheet submitted within the deadline set by the superintendent of police. He added that the accused were arrested within 24 hours of the recovery of the body and that the case had been investigated with due importance.
Court proceedings did not begin immediately after the charge sheet was submitted because of the government holidays for Durga Puja. Police sources said court activities were scheduled to resume on Sunday after the holidays.
Apratim went missing on September 18 after leaving his home in the Gandhamati area of Kotbari in Cumilla city. He was a Class VII student at Border Guard Public School in Kotbari.
Police recovered his body the following day, September 19, from an isolated forest in the Lalm AI hills in Sananda village under Bijoypur Union of Sadar Dakshin upazila.
According to investigators, Apratim was taken to the isolated location as part of a plan to steal his iPhone. When he resisted the attempt to take the phone, he was struck on the head with a bamboo stick, causing his death, police said.
Investigators said they identified Tuhin after reviewing CCTV footage from several locations. Questioning him subsequently led police to information about the involvement of others, they added.
Police also said Apratim’s iPhone was recovered from beneath a mattress at Tuhin’s home based on information provided by him.
Three people, including Tuhin, were initially arrested in connection with the murder. Siam was arrested later after investigators found evidence of his alleged involvement.
With the submission of the charge sheet, the investigation has reached a significant milestone. Apratim’s family is now awaiting the start of the trial and hopes the court will ensure justice and punish those found guilty in accordance with the law.

item.title: New colours, old buses as Dhaka prepares another transport overhaul
Two killed, 2 hurt in motorcycle collision in Pabna
item.description:
Two people were killed and two others injured in a head-on collision between two motorcycles in the Jalalpur area of Pabna Sadar upazila on Thursday night.
The deceased were identified as Nayon Mia, 20, son of Abdul Matin Mridha of Shalaipur village under Gayeshpur union, and Selim Mahmud, 40, son of late Mozaffar Hossain of Jalalpur village.
The accident occurred around 8pm near Jalalpur Bazar, said Monirul Islam, Sub-Inspector of Pabna Sadar Police Station.
Citing locals, police said the two motorcycles collided head-on while travelling at high speed on the road between Jalalpur and Gayeshpur, leaving two people dead and two others injured.
The injured persons were initially taken to Pabna General Hospital. Later, one of them was shifted to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital as his condition deteriorated.
On receiving information, police rushed to the spot and recovered the bodies.

item.title: Truck driver held with 800 litres of fuel in Aminbazar
item.description:
Police have detained a truck driver for allegedly smuggling 800 litres of diesel meant for excavator operations at the Dhaka North City Corporation’s (DNCC) landfill in Aminbazar, Savar.
The truck used to transport the fuel was also seized.
The driver, identified as Al-Amin, 34, was detained on Thursday night near Salehpur Bridge in Aminbazar on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway.
Al-Amin is from Barisal. He lives in a rented house in the Godarghat area of Mirpur-1 in Dhaka and works as a driver of a garbage-carrying drum truck for the city corporation.
According to police, officers were conducting routine checks on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in Aminbazar on Thursday night when they stopped a truck carrying 40 containers of diesel, totalling 800 litres, towards Dhaka.
Police searched the truck and seized the fuel and the vehicle, detaining the driver on suspicion of smuggling.
Aminbazar Police Camp In-charge Zakir Al Ahsan, who is under Savar Model police station, said the driver admitted to smuggling the fuel during initial interrogation.
He said the driver was transporting the government-owned diesel from the Aminbazar landfill to a fuel-smuggling syndicate in Mohammadpur, Dhaka.
Legal action is under way, the police official added.

item.title: Eight years after safe roads movement, deaths keep mounting
Dhaka's air quality remains 'unhealthy'
item.description:
Dhaka's air quality remained unhealthy on Friday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 153 at 9:10am.
With this score, the capital ranked 12th among the world's most polluted cities.
Pakistan's Lahore, India's Delhi and Senegal's Dakar occupied the top three spots on the list, with AQI scores of 344, 244 and 184 respectively.
Earlier, at 9:20 am on Thursday, the city ranked 7th among the world's most polluted cities, recording an AQI score of 165.
An AQI score between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate" with acceptable air quality, while one between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups," and a score between 151 and 200 is classified as "unhealthy."
AQI readings between 201 and 300 are termed "very unhealthy," and anything above 301 is considered "hazardous," posing serious health risks.
The AQI is a daily indicator of air quality, showing how clean or polluted the air is and the possible health effects people may experience.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone.

Taskin returns as Bangladesh name squad for West Indies
item.description:
Bangladesh have named their squad for the opening match of their ICC World Test Championship series at home against the West Indies.
The side have been boosted by the return of experienced pacer Taskin Ahmed for the opening Test of the two-game series that commences in Mirpur on 28 October, with the right-armer named in the 15-player squad after he missed the one-off Test against Afghanistan at the start of this month.
Najmul Hossain Shanto will captain the side throughout the series as Bangladesh look to continue their push towards next year's World Test Championship Final, while experienced batter Litton Das is included in the squad despite a recent hip injury.
Bangladesh currently sit in fourth place on the World Test Championship standings and will be looking for a pair of positive results against the West Indies as they try and move towards a top two berth and a spot in the 2027 final.
Bangladesh squad: Najmul Hossain Shanto (c), Taskin Ahmed, Jaker Ali Anik, Litton Das, Mominul Haque, Nayeem Hasan, Tanzid Hasan, Ebadot Hossain Chowdhury, Tawhid Hridoy, Shadman Islam, Shoriful Islam, Taijul Islam, Hasan Mahmud, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Mushfiqur Rahim

item.title: Bournemouth hammer 10-man Milan, Juventus denied at the death
item.description:
Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League.
Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC Milan, one of Europe's leading clubs.
Milan goalkeeper and skipper Mike Maignan was red carded early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never fully recovered.
Amine Adli scored a sublime 84th free-kick to make it 3-0, the Premier League side having opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad followed by a 3-0 home win over Sturm Graz last week.
Bournemouth, who became the first English club since Sunderland in 1973/74 to win the first three European fixtures in their history, will now face Sparta Prague and Celta Vigo in November.
"It means a lot. We came off two victories, so that gave us a good feeling for this game," Kluivert told TNT Sports.
"We trust ourselves. It doesn't matter who we play against. We know what we're capable of, and I think we showed that today."
Bournemouth's Premier League rivals Crystal Palace rebounded from a 5-0 weekend thrashing by Brighton to claim a 2-2 draw with Beskitas in Istanbul, while Scottish giants Celtic suffered a third successive defeat, going down 2-1 to Celta Vigo.
Bayer Leverkusen, however, also made it three straight wins with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday's third matchday.
The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium's Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be'er Sheva.
Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games.
Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late 'winner' ruled out for a marginal offside.
Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead.
Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi's 88th minute strike.
Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland.
The Blacks Cats took a second minute lead in Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win.
With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris' side.
Marseille went down 1-0 to Sturn Graz while Lyon suffered a 3-0 thrashing at the hands of Hoffenheim.
In the Conference League, former Liverpool striker Mohamed Salah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in Trabzonspor's 2-0 win over Scottish side Hearts.
Brighton were held to a 0-0 draw at Czech side Jablonec, as Monaco thumped Freiburg 3-0 and Ajax snuck a 2-0 win over Atalanta.

item.title: Pacers power Proteas to series-levelling win over Australia
item.description:
Travis Head’s defiant century provided stirring resistance, but South Africa's relentless bowling attack dismantled Australia’s lower order on a blockbuster Day 5 to secure a comprehensive win by an innings and 31 runs in the second Test.
The win in Gqeberha levels the three-match ICC World Test Championship series 1-1, setting up an exciting conclusion to the WTC series.
After early weather interruptions disrupted the opening two days of the fixture, South Africa seized total control through skipper Temba Bavuma’s monumental 179 and a record-breaking 183-run eighth-wicket partnership with Simon Harmer (82) that propelled the hosts to a formidable 425/9 declared.
Marco Jansen’s devastating spell of 5/33 then skittled Australia for just 99 in their first innings, forcing the visitors to follow on.
South Africa then enforced the follow-on as Australia lost quick wickets before finishing the penultimate day at 156/4.
Resuming play on the final morning with an innings defeat looming, Australia pinned their hopes on Travis Head.
Head, who played with supreme authority against both pace and spin, went on to score a century, extending his overnight score to a magnificent 121 off 190 deliveries, striking 15 boundaries.
Accompanying him at the other end, Scott Boland also produced a characteristically gritty rear-guard action, occupying the crease for 166 balls for his 40 runs, but Kagiso Rabada and Wiaan Mulder maintained relentless pressure.
Rabada, who finished with superb figures of 4/77, broke through the resistance with searing pace and accuracy, while Mulder chipped in with 3/64.
Simon Harmer also wrapped up ends expertly with his off-spin, as South Africa eventually bowled Australia out for 295 in 107.1 overs.
The emphatic victory provides a significant boost to South Africa’s standing in the ICC World Test Championship 2025–27 standings.
Having entered the match sitting third behind leaders Australia and second-placed New Zealand, the Proteas added 12 crucial points to boost their points percentage (PCT) back up to 66.67%, solidifying their position in the top three and closing the gap on Australia, who maintain their lead at the top of the table despite their percentage slipping to 75.00%.
With the series now squared at 1-1, both sides head to Cape Town for a blockbuster series decider.
Series schedule
First Test: 9-13 October, Durban (Australia won by 214 runs)
Second Test: 18-22 October, Gqeberha
Third Test: 27-31 October, Cape Town

item.title: India complete record chase to beat New Zealand
item.description:
Sanju Samson's blistering half-century put India on course before a sensational finishing masterclass by Naman Dhir secured a thrilling four-wicket victory over New Zealand in the opening T20I at Hagley Oval, taking a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.
Chasing a daunting target of 226, India pulled off their highest-ever successful run chase in T20I history, reaching 230/6 with two balls to spare.
While Samson's 33-ball 67 anchored the top order and laid a formidable foundation, a mid-innings collapse threatened to derail the visitors before Dhir's power-hitting 15-ball 42* got them across the line in a high-octane Christchurch thriller.
Reflecting on the record-breaking pursuit, the performance underscored India's depth under pressure on a true Hagley Oval surface where boundaries flowed freely throughout the evening.
New Zealand had earlier set a formidable total of 225/4 after Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to field. The Blackcaps top order set a relentless pace from the outset, with Finn Allen kickstarting the fireworks via a quickfire 45 off 24 deliveries alongside Tim Seifert.
While India managed brief breakthroughs through Mayank Yadav and Axar Patel, Glenn Phillips seized total control of the middle and death overs.
Displaying exceptional power and timing, Phillips smashed an unbeaten 82 from just 40 balls, striking eight boundaries and three maximums. Supported by Daryl Mitchell's brisk 28 off 19, Phillips propelled the hosts past the 220-run mark.
India's response began in blistering fashion. Opening the innings, Samson and Abhishek Sharma wasted no time, plundering 68 runs in the first four overs to keep the required rate firmly in check.
Samson was in pristine touch, reaching his half-century in style and dictating terms against the pace attack.
However, New Zealand fought back fiercely through their spin options. Michael Bracewell broke the opening stand by removing Abhishek for 29, before Blackcaps skipper Mitchell Santner struck twice in quick succession to remove Samson and Ishan Kishan.
From a comfortable 93/0, India suddenly found themselves reeling at 122/4 midway through the chase.
With the required run rate steadily climbing, Shreyas Iyer (42 off 28) and Axar Patel (24 off 14) combined to reignite India's hopes, launching a 20-run counter-attack against Matt Henry in the 14th over.
When Iyer fell in the penultimate over with 15 runs still required, Naman Dhir stepped up to the plate.
The right-hander produced a breathtaking, unbeaten cameo, dispatching the bowling with supreme confidence.
Needing just three runs from the final four deliveries, Dhir launched Henry over deep fine leg for a maximum to seal a historic victory for the visitors.

item.title: Sri Lanka stun England with huge chase after Brook's double century
item.description:
Janith Liyanage smashed a six off the penultimate ball as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, scoring 430-8 to beat England in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
Needing eight to win off the last over, Sri Lanka lost two wickets to paceman Josh Tongue, but Liyanage kept his cool to achieve an astonishing victory and overshadow Harry Brook's record-setting knock.
The England captain hit the fastest-ever ODI double hundred, making 202 off 116 balls to propel his team to a mammoth 429-4 after they were put in to bat.
South Africa hold the record for the highest ODI chase, knocking off a target of 435 against Australia at Johannesburg in 2006.
Batters thoroughly dominated in Rawalpindi as Brook also hit the first ODI double century by an England player. However, Sri Lanka proved up to the challenge as Pavan Rathnayake scored 130, with Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both making 97.
Liyanage then led them over the line with a blistering 61 not out off 27 balls.
Sri Lanka slid to 24-2 before Rathnayake and Avishka set about transforming the innings, putting on 166 for the third wicket.
Rathnayake then combined with Shanaka to lift the tempo with a rapid 133-run stand off just 79 balls, to give Sri Lanka genuine hope.
Rathnayake hit 15 fours and three sixes while Shanaka's blazing knock featured eight sixes and six fours, as Sri Lanka delivered a powerful response to Brook's earlier masterclass.
Sri Lankan skipper Kusal Mendis was delighted at victory.
"I'm very happy as a captain," said Mendis. "Everyone believed we can do it. Every day we talk about showing the character in team meetings, and it's about showing we can get any score."
Brook was full of praise for Sri Lanka.
"Incredible game of cricket, both teams were exceptional. They played exceptional cricket to knock off 400," said Brook, downplaying his double hundred.
"It was a nice innings but being on the losing side it has no value whatsoever in my eyes."
Brook clobbered 10 sixes and 21 fours as England posted a first 400-plus ODI total in Pakistan.
He reached 200 in 114 balls, beating the previous fastest double century in ODIs, by Shubman Gill (117 balls) for India against West Indies last month.
Brook was joined in the fireworks by Joe Root, who scored a 66-ball 69 and became the first England batter to complete 8,000 runs, in his 197th one-day international.
Brook was dismissed off the final delivery, caught off paceman Liyanage, but not before helping England add 156 runs in the last 10 overs.
Opener Tom Banton set the tone with a 51-ball 50 and Will Jacks was 66 not out with three sixes and eight fours.
The day looked as if it would surely belong to history-maker Brook, but Sri Lanka had other ideas as the previous highest ODI total at a Pakistan venue of 375-3 was easily surpassed.
Pakistan, who beat Sri Lanka and England in their two games, will face England in Lahore on Sunday in the next match in the tri-series.

item.title: Maradona doctor was made 'scapegoat' for his death, Argentine court told
Little care for healthcare
item.description:
A recent report documenting 7,500 patients waiting for radiotherapy due to a shortage of treatment facilities and capacity at National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH) is deeply concerning.
Every little delay can allow a disease to progress, reduce the chances of recovery, and place an even greater burden on families already struggling to cope, making this a matter of life and death.
The situation becomes more troubling when we consider how many Bangladeshis seek treatment abroad because they lack confidence in, or access to, adequate medical care at home.
However, travelling overseas is not a realistic option for most citizens. The costs of treatment, travel, and accommodation are prohibitive, while visa restrictions, the need for medical attendants, and the urgency of treatment create additional barriers.
This is not something to be taken lightly. Immediate action must begin with making the most of existing resources. The government should assess the availability and operational status of radiotherapy machines across public hospitals, repair non-functional equipment, and extend operating hours where staffing and safety permit.
Patients waiting for treatment should be registered in a centralized system and referred to facilities with available capacity. Partnerships with private hospitals could also help provide subsidized treatment to patients who cannot afford private healthcare.
Public hospitals must receive adequate funding, while transparent procurement and maintenance systems should prevent expensive equipment from remaining unused.
Cancer care, and indeed good healthcare in general, must not become a privilege reserved for those who can afford to cross borders. The government has a responsibility to ensure that citizens can access timely, quality treatment within their own country.
Promises of better healthcare mean little when patients spend their most critical days waiting. Every day lost is a day that some patients may never get back.

item.title: Prioritizing the rule of law
item.description:
The latest findings from the World Justice Project (WJP) Rule of Law Index 2026, which places Bangladesh at an abysmal 123rd out of 143 countries, should serve as an urgent wake-up call.
While the improvement from 125th last year is positive, and potentially shows that we are heading in the right direction, this marginal, fractional improvement does not change our reality, which remains humiliating.
That Bangladesh continues to trail behind several African nations, including Kenya, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe, and is languishing near the bottom of regional and global governance metrics shows that there is little to be proud of for us. Instead, it is time for some much needed humility, and the need to get to work.
There is no denying that there has been a structural decay when it comes to ensuring fundamental rights and civil justice in recent years. While minor gains were logged in governmental constraints and regulatory enforcement, fundamental rights plummeted to 133rd globally, placing Bangladesh among the lowest-ranked nations for protecting basic human freedoms.
Similarly, civil justice ranked a dismal 132nd, demonstrating that access to effective remedies and impartial dispute resolution remains an empty promise for ordinary citizens.
When a country's judicial and legal frameworks fail to guarantee basic security, equity, and civil protection, it is the entire nation and its people that bear the ramifications.
We cannot take comfort in sluggish, incremental movements when systemic rot continues to paralyze our institutions. We must recognize and address the bureaucratic inertia, selective legal enforcement, and political interference that have corroded the judiciary and law enforcement bodies.
Talk of reform continues to fall on deaf years, yet comprehensive, aggressive institutional reforms remain more urgent than ever before. Bangladesh will never reach its potential as a nation without restoring public trust. For that, the rule of law must apply equally to all.

item.title: Debates that never happened
item.description:
Imagine scrolling through YouTube at midnight and meeting a split screen. Sheikh Hasina sits on one side, Jamaat Ameer Dr Shafiqur Rahman on the other, and the title promises a face-to-face clash on Khaled Muhiuddin’s talk show.
More than 352,000 viewers watched it, and thousands argued in the comments as if they had witnessed live television. They had not. No studio, no host, and no debate ever existed.
A second video was bolder still. Its caption said Hasanul Haq Inu was speaking live right after leaving jail while Prime Minister Tarique Rahman listened. In reality, editors arranged old footage to mimic a real-time exchange, and Inu has been in custody since 2024.
Both clips are cheapfakes: No artificial intelligence, just cutting, a split screen, and a trusted program’s borrowed look.
Neither case is an accident. A recent study by FactWatch identified around 300 similar items and then examined several platforms.
According to findings, the YouTube channel Rajnoitik Studio and the Facebook page Bangla News240 collectively published more than 300 fabricated shows that accumulated roughly 517K followers.
The fabricated broadcasts typically target sensitive political topics, elections, or public controversies to shape public opinion or push partisan agendas. The casting is telling. Fabricated statements and deepfakes regularly target key political leadership.
Why does the talk-show format work so well? A studio duel squeezes messy politics into a contest anyone can follow, and the host lends borrowed authority. A reel then strips away the channel behind it, so viewers see a clip, not its source. People struggle most when fakes wear a news format.
By combining psychological manipulation with media impersonation, these AI-generated “talk shows” and deepfakes weaponize local cultural sensitivities to shift public opinion. A single deepfake is easy to ignore, but hundreds of them create an illusion of reality.
If a viewer scrolls and sees others echoing the same political talking point, they begin to believe that the entire country feels that way.
One fake show persuades a few people; a hundred of them feel like a national mood.
Prof Sumon Rahman, founding editor of FactWatch, has warned that confirmation bias and timing can confuse even media-literate viewers.
This is a tactic of manufactured majoritarianism. A report reveals that nearly 30,000 fake reactions were purchased from four click farms. They cost roughly Tk 120 to 200 per thousand, and some arrived within minutes. A review of 263 posts counted 885,811 reactions, 62% of them “haha,” and at least 19,708 came from bot-like profiles.
“How artificial intelligence and synthetic reality shaped Bangladesh’s 2026 election,” a study concluded that coordinated narrative manipulation had become a structural feature, introduced with Bangladesh’s first AI-saturated election, where seeing was no longer believing.
No single mastermind appears in the record. Instead, several actors overlap. The click-farm probe found politically aligned clusters moving in tandem, yet it did not examine official party links. The administrators of those talk-show channels never answered the questions.
Some operators work alone. Anthropic’s September threat report, relayed by bdnews24, described one operator in Gaibandha who rotated 29 AI accounts over about 16 months and produced roughly 1,500 fake headlines. The company found no evidence that the Awami League ran or funded the network.
Others are plainly commercial.
FactWatch exposed a counterfeit Prothom Alo page with an invented interview with Abdullah Abu Sayeed that steered readers toward a trading platform; meanwhile, the Daily Star documented 52 deepfake videos and 31 pages offering fake Family Cards for likes.
Consequently, “who” is less a mastermind than a marketplace.
FactWatch’s data offers a before-and-after picture. In its 2024 election study , video made up 71.9% of 157 unique hoaxes, and only three, or 1.9%, were deepfakes.
By 2026, another analysis of 72 AI-manipulated cases found that 49% invented what leaders did or said, and 28% used AI-edited photocards to fake quotes.
After Osman Hadi was shot on December 12, 2025, fact-checkers documented within two days fake photocards in the names of RTV, Kalbela, BBC Bangla, and Amar Desh, an AI image of a suspect, and an AI clip in which a hand grips a man yet belongs to no one.
A widely shared photograph of Shadik Kayem with the suspect was synthetic, yet BNP’s Ruhul Kabir Rizvi cited it at a rally and later apologized.
For years, the standard advice has been to tell citizens to verify before sharing. That advice is sound, yet it is unfair on its own. A viewer on a bus, with a phone and little data, cannot reverse-search a split screen.
After the Cyber Security Act of April 2026, draft amendments would force platforms to remove harmful AI content, and Transparency International Bangladesh and other rights groups fear a return to Digital Security Act-style repression.
A vague takedown power is easily aimed at critics, and real journalism can also be dismissed as fake. Any rule should therefore target fraud, impersonation, and paid fake engagement, with judicial review and public reporting, rather than “misinformation” in general.
Broadcasters and newsrooms have a duty. Every outlet whose face or microphone is borrowed should publish a quick, searchable “this is not ours” notice, and should consider visible watermarks on original clips.
The click-farm evidence shows that candidates from several parties share the same bot pool. A public pledge never to buy engagement, never to circulate unverified cards, and to apologize quickly when fooled would cost nothing. Rizvi’s apology was a start; it should become a norm.
Return, finally, to that midnight scroll. The harm of a fake talk show is not only that someone believes a debate occurred.
Political factions in Bangladesh do not just create fake videos for entertainment; they use them to manufacture deliberate, high-stakes narratives.
A falsehood once believed does not stay online. It walks into real politics.
A studio that never existed can cost a few hours and a laptop. Rebuilding trust in real ones will cost far more.
Zulker Naeen is a Research Coordinator, Centre for Critical and Qualitative Studies (CQS) and Adjunct Faculty, Department of Media Studies and Journalism (MSJ), University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB). Views expressed are the writer’s own.

item.title: Dhaka-Chittagong rail services resume after 24 hours
item.description:
Train services on the Dhaka-bound line of the Dhaka-Chittagong route resumed at 12:50pm on Thursday, more than 24 hours after the Karnaphuli Commuter Express derailed in Comilla's Laksam.
The Bijoy Express, travelling from Chittagong to Mymensingh, was the first train to cross the accident site after the line reopened.
Omar Faruk Bhuiyan, station master of Laksam Railway Junction, said train services were now operating normally on both lines.
The damaged track was repaired by 7am on Thursday, but services remained suspended on the Dhaka-bound line because a derailed coach was found. During the suspension, trains in both directions used the other line, causing some disruption. The Chattala Express, bound for Dhaka, and the Paharika Express, bound for Sylhet, passed through Laksam at 10:23am and 10:48am, respectively, on Thursday.
The accident occurred around 12:30pm on Wednesday in the outer section of Naoti station, near Azgara Bazar in Laksam, when five coaches of the Karnaphuli Commuter Express and three wheels of its engine derailed. At least seven passengers were injured.
A rescue train from Chittagong reached the site on Wednesday evening. Recovery work was completed around 5am on Thursday, followed by track repairs.
Meanwhile, railway authorities suspended sub-assistant engineer Sarwar Alam over allegations that he failed to inform the control room about repair work underway at the accident site. He was responsible for the Feni region under the Eastern Railway’s engineering department.
A four-member committee has been formed to investigate the accident, Chittagong Divisional Railway Manager Mostafizur Rahman Bhuiyan said on Wednesday night.

item.title: Bangladesh ambassador to stay in Dhaka during PM’s Japan visit
item.description:
Bangladesh’s Ambassador to Japan Md Daud Ali will remain in Dhaka during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s upcoming visit to Japan, with Ministry of Foreign Affairs Secretary Md Nazrul Islam set to oversee preparations and arrangements in Tokyo.
Sources at the ministry said the ambassador would not accompany the prime minister on the visit. Md Daud Ali is currently in Dhaka on the instructions of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
However, a ministry official told Dhaka Tribune on Thursday that the ambassador was in Dhaka due to illness. Whether he would join the prime minister’s visit to Japan would be known after his leave.
The prime minister is scheduled to visit Tokyo from October 26 to 29.
According to relevant sources, Secretary Md Nazrul Islam will stay in Tokyo in the ambassador’s absence and oversee preparations and arrangements for the prime minister’s visit.
Nazrul Islam left Dhaka for Tokyo on Wednesday, October 21, to carry out the responsibilities assigned to him for the visit. He will remain there until the visit concludes.
According to diplomats, it is unusual for an ambassador to be in Dhaka on the instructions of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs ahead of a prime ministerial visit.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,207 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Thursday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,207.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified both of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,103, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the two new suspected fatalities, both were recorded in Dhaka.
A total of 995 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Thursday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 217,760.
During the same period, 36 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 23,248.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 193,608 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 185,927 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: 4,157 killed in nine months as nation marks Road Safety Day
item.description:
Twelve people died in a head-on collision in Natore on Tuesday. According to police and surviving passengers, the bus was being driven by its supervisor while the regular driver slept in the back.
Two days later, Bangladesh is observing National Road Safety Day with the familiar program of seminars, discussions and promises to make its roads safer.
The latest figures offer little reason for reassurance.
At least 4,157 people were killed and 5,391 injured in 4,285 road crashes between January and September this year, according to the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA). That is an average of more than 15 deaths every day.
This year’s observance, under the theme “Safe Roads, Prosperous Nation, Bangladesh First,” comes amid persistent concerns over unfit vehicles, unqualified drivers and the failure to enforce existing traffic laws.
The Natore crash brought several of those concerns into sharp focus.
Police and injured passengers said the RP Special Paribahan bus was heading towards Bonpara when its supervisor, Sohel Rana, took over the wheel after a stop at Ishwardi around 3am.
Ramjan Ali, a surviving passenger from Chapainawabganj, said the regular driver left his seat after the break. About an hour later, the bus collided with a truck, killing 12 people and injuring at least 25.
The circumstances of the crash have once again raised questions about who is allowed to drive passenger buses and how effectively transport operators are monitored.
The deaths in Natore are part of a much larger toll.
According to Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity, at least 125,405 people were killed in 72,736 road crashes between 2013 and 2025. Another 176,249 people were left permanently disabled, the organisation said.
Children have been among the worst affected. Road Safety Foundation figures show that 7,963 children died in road crashes between January 2020 and September 2026.
Nearly 3,000 of them were killed in motorcycle crashes, while 2,812 died as pedestrians.
Yet the problems identified by successive governments and road safety experts remain largely unresolved.
BRTA records indicate that around 650,000 vehicles are operating without the required registration, route permits or fitness certificates. More than 75,000 buses and trucks have exceeded their prescribed economic lifespan.
The shortage of qualified professional drivers for heavy and medium vehicles is estimated at around 30%.
Vehicle fitness is another major concern. Around 70% of buses and minibuses in Dhaka and other major cities reportedly lack valid fitness documents.
Driver health also receives inadequate attention. At a BRTA and Dhaka Ahsania Mission health camp in 2023, around 73% of 541 drivers who underwent eye examinations were found to need glasses.
In 2019, the National Road Safety Council identified seven priority areas and made 111 recommendations to improve road safety.
Experts say there has been little visible progress in implementing them.
BUET Assistant Professor Kazi Md Saifun Newaz said the country already has the Road Transport Act 2018 and Road Transport Rules 2022, but legislation alone cannot prevent crashes.
“Everyone knows the causes of road crashes and their remedies. What is missing is consistent and coordinated action,” he said.
“Observing days will not solve anything.”
The BRTA says it has filed more than 110,000 cases through mobile courts and joint enforcement drives in the first nine months of this year, targeting unfit vehicles, invalid licences, speeding and other violations.
But the continuing death toll raises questions about whether these drives are producing lasting improvements.
Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity Secretary General Mozammel Haque Chowdhury blamed institutional inefficiency, corruption and the influence of transport owners’ and workers’ groups for the persistent disorder.
Road Safety Foundation Executive Director Saidur Rahman said the dangers were particularly acute for children on rural roads, where vehicles frequently pass close to homes and enforcement is weak.
“The authorities know the causes and the consequences, but there is no remedy,” he said.
The government has pledged to enact a comprehensive road safety law by December 2027.
The proposed Road Safety Act 2026 includes free emergency treatment for crash victims, legal protection for people who assist the injured, a demerit-point system for traffic offenders and higher penalties for repeat violations.
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam has also reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to the UN target of halving road deaths and serious injuries by 2030.
For now, the country enters another Road Safety Day with thousands of lives lost, longstanding recommendations awaiting implementation and another deadly crash exposing the dangers on its highways.

item.title: Man beaten to death at Dhaka hospital over child theft suspicion
item.description:
A 41-year-old man was beaten to death at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital in Dhaka on suspicion of being a child kidnapper.
The incident took place in front of the hospital’s children’s ward around 11pm on Wednesday. Police have detained a man in connection with the incident.
Police said Md Alam Sheikh was loitering in front of the children’s ward when relatives of children receiving treatment there became suspicious of him and questioned his presence at the hospital.
As he allegedly failed to provide a satisfactory explanation, several people dragged him downstairs and beat him, leaving him critically injured. He died early Thursday.
Police said they went to the scene after receiving an alert through the national emergency service 999. Alam’s identity was later confirmed through fingerprint verification.
He was from Natore. Police have contacted his family members, who are on their way to Dhaka.
Deputy Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Tejgaon Division, Ibne Mizan said the body had been sent to the morgue of Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College for an autopsy.
He said one person had been detained in connection with the incident. He added that legal action will be taken if the victim’s family files a complaint with the police.

item.title: Shibir says youth detained over PM comment is not a member
item.description:
Islami Chhatra Shibir has denied that Abu Bakar Siddique, 22, detained over a Facebook comment about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to Rajshahi, is a member of the organization.
Imran Nazir, president of the Rajshahi metropolitan unit of Islami Chhatra Shibir, said: “There is an attempt to put the blame on Shibir whenever something happens. But Abu Bakar Siddique is not one of our members.”
Abu Bakar was detained on Wednesday afternoon at his maternal uncle’s house in Gholharia village in Hatrāmchandrapur, Paba upazila, Rajshahi. His father, Ainal Haque, was also detained during the operation. Both are now in the custody of the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
Chandrima police station Officer-in-Charge Monirul Islam said police had found no information indicating whether Abu Bakar had previously been arrested or whether any case had been filed against him. His political affiliation was also unknown, he added.
Mahmud Hasan Limon, president of the Chhatra Dal unit at Rajshahi New Government Degree College, said: “I heard from people in the administration that Abu Bakar used to be involved with the Chhatra League. Now, apparently, he is involved with Chhatra Shibir. But I have not seen anything at the college. We did not really know him.”
Shariful Islam, an assistant professor in the History Department of Rajshahi New Government Degree College, said Abu Bakar was a regular student who had taken his first-year final examinations, although the results had not yet been published. He said he had not observed any misconduct by Abu Bakar at the college.
After learning about the Facebook comment, Shariful Islam spoke to several students. According to him, they said Abu Bakar’s father had previously supported the Awami League but had been associating with Jamaat-e-Islami since August 5.
Shariful Islam also said he had heard that Abu Bakar had been involved with the Bangladesh Chhatra League through his family, although he had not observed any such involvement at the college.
The Facebook comment appeared under a photograph of the prime minister posted by a page named “The Beauty of Rajshahi.” The account, bearing the name Abu Bakar Siddique, commented: “What a great opportunity. Only a sniper was missing.”
During his visit to Rajshahi on Tuesday, Tarique Rahman traveled on a Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology (RUET) bus from the airport to Madrasa Maidan and then to Dharmasabha before returning to the airport. Large numbers of people lined both sides of the road to greet him, and he responded to their greetings.
Following the comment, law enforcement agencies launched an operation to identify the account holder.
According to local residents, a team from the Cyber Crime Unit of Rajshahi Metropolitan Police and Chandrima police station went to Abu Bakar’s house at around 2pm on Wednesday. He was not there, and his family members did not disclose his whereabouts.
At around 4pm, a team from SRB-5 arrived at the house in plain clothes. Unable to find Abu Bakar, the team detained his father for questioning. Ainal Haque subsequently told them that his son was staying at his maternal uncle’s house in Gholharia village.
SRB-5 members then took Ainal Haque to the house and detained Abu Bakar. A mobile phone used by the family was seized, and both were subsequently handed over to the DMP’s Detective Branch.
SRB-5 Commander Lieutenant Colonel Faisal Ishtiaq confirmed the handover, saying: “We have handed both of them over to the DB. They will provide further details about the matter later.”
Abu Bakar lives in the Kechuatail area under Chandrima police station in Rajshahi city. His father, a farmer, has 4 children, with Abu Bakar being the eldest.
On Thursday morning, Monirul Islam searched Abu Bakar’s house. After nearly an hour, police found no evidence worth seizing apart from the packaging of a pen drive.
Police also attempted to recover Abu Bakar’s laptop, but family members said he neither used nor owned one.

item.title: Six law enforcers injured as gunfire targets Sajek tourist convoy
item.description:
Six members of law enforcement agencies were injured in an attack on a tourist convoy amid a road blockade on the Sajek-Baghaihat road in Rangamati’s Baghaichhari upazila on Thursday morning.
The incident occurred in the Ujobaazar area, prompting the army and police to evacuate the tourists to safety.
Rangamati Superintendent of Police Muhammad Abdur Rakib disclosed the details at a press conference at his office around 2:00pm on Thursday.
He said the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association had enforced a road blockade from October 11 to 15. The programme was suspended from October 16 to 21 for Durga Puja, with plans to resume it thereafter.
The blockade left 2,933 tourists stranded in Sajek, the SP said.
To ensure their safe return, a convoy of tourist vehicles left Sajek around 9:00am on Thursday under the security escort of the Bangladesh army and police.
When the convoy reached Ujobaazar around 10:00am, law enforcement personnel held talks with the protesters to facilitate the tourists’ safe passage. The protesters then hurled bricks and stones at the security personnel, injuring six members, Abdur Rakib said.
The protesters were subsequently removed from the road, allowing the convoy to proceed.
Based on intelligence reports, authorities later learned that an armed group affiliated with the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF) had opened fire targeting the tourist convoy, the SP said.
Law enforcement personnel returned fire to protect the tourists and safeguard public property, he added.
Intermittent exchanges of gunfire between the armed group and law enforcement personnel continued even after the tourists had been moved to safety.
The gunfight lasted from around 11:00am to 1:00pm, after which the situation came under control, Abdur Rakib said.
Md Jasim Uddin, a Mahindra driver on the Sajek route, said they left Sajek around 9:00am under a security escort.
“They were stopped by protesters at Ujobaazar around 10:00am and remained stranded for about 40 minutes. Later, security personnel dispersed the protesters using batons, allowing us to continue,” he said.
He said they reached Khagrachhari around 12:40pm.
Rahul Chakma John, organising secretary of the Sajek Cottage and Resort Owners Association, said around 3,000 tourists had returned from Sajek to Khagrachhari.
On Wednesday, Sajek Karbari Association President Natun Joy Chakma and Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee Convener Babudhan Chakma announced in a joint statement that an indefinite road blockade would resume from Thursday.
The organisations alleged that armed members of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana-Samhati Samiti (JSS-Santu Larma) were active in different parts of Sajek.
They also alleged that the armed members had threatened and intimidated local residents, forced some people to leave their homes and seized mobile phones from villagers.
As a result, ordinary Jum farmers were unable to tend to their gardens, the organisations claimed.
They said the blockade would continue until the alleged armed members were removed from the area and measures were taken to ensure the safety and security of local residents.
Natun Joy Chakma said talks were underway with law enforcement agencies but they would not withdraw the blockade unless their three demands were addressed.
He said the blockade had been suspended from October 16 to 21 in observance of Durga Puja.
However, he alleged that the administration did not hold any discussions with them during that period.
He said tourists staying in Sajek had also been given sufficient time to leave, prompting them to resume the blockade as announced.
The indefinite blockade on the Sajek Road was initially launched on October 11 and suspended from October 16 to 21 for Durga Puja. With the blockade resuming on Thursday, concerns have resurfaced over tourist movement and security in Sajek.
According to local accounts, while the Bangladesh Army was escorting around 3,000 stranded tourists to safety, armed members of the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF), along with women participating in the blockade, allegedly hurled bricks and stones at the tourists in the Gongaram Bazar area of Sajek.
The incident occurred as the tourists were being escorted out of the area amid the ongoing blockade.

item.title: Fire at Rangpur Medical College Hospital injures 40 patients
item.description:
At least 40 patients and their relatives were injured while rushing to evacuate Rangpur Medical College Hospital after a fire broke out due to a short circuit on Thursday morning.
The fire originated from a switchboard near the administrative section of the hospital’s electrical control room on the ground floor around 6:15am.
Firefighters quickly brought the blaze under control, but the hospital remained without electricity for six hours, triggering panic among patients and their attendants.
The power outage disrupted medical services, forcing the suspension of emergency surgeries and other treatments. Although partial power was restored to several wards after prolonged efforts, the nephrology, cardiology, gynaecology and kidney dialysis wards remained without electricity.
According to patients, hospital authorities and fire service officials, panic spread throughout the hospital as patients and their relatives rushed to leave the building. Those staying in wards on the second to fifth floors hurried down the stairs, with many falling and sustaining injuries. At least 40 people were injured in falls during the rush to evacuate the hospital.
As of 4pm, the offices of the hospital director, cardiology department, pathology ward, dermatology and venereology ward, kidney dialysis ward and nephrology ward remained without electricity, leaving patients struggling in the intense heat.
During a visit to the hospital, patients described the chaos surrounding the evacuation.
Shafiul Alam, a kidney patient receiving treatment in the second-floor nephrology ward, was being carried downstairs when his two nephews fell and were injured. Shafiul was also hurt in the incident.
At least 15 patients in the ward were injured while rushing downstairs, with some reportedly trampled in the crowd.
Several infants were also injured as patients and their attendants rushed down the stairs from the third-floor gynaecology ward with newborns.
Mamtaz Begum, a patient in the gynaecology ward, said her baby girl was born five days ago. After hearing about the fire, she rushed downstairs with her newborn and was injured during the evacuation.
Many others used the emergency exit stairs to escape, with several sustaining injuries in the rush.
Deputy Director of Rangpur Medical College Hospital Dr Md Abdul Mokaddem said the fire was caused by a short circuit.
“Efforts are underway to restore electricity to all wards,” he said.

The Climate Watch to deploy eight journalists at COP31
item.description:
As global attention turns to the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, Bangladeshi news organization The Climate Watch is preparing to bring South Asia’s climate struggles, demands and stories to the international stage.
Officially launched on November 3, 2024, The Climate Watch will deploy 8 journalists from Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka to cover the UN climate summit, scheduled for November 9-20. The team comprises 5 full-time journalists and 3 regional contributors, marking the publication’s largest international reporting operation to date.
While financial pressures have forced several established Western news organizations to reduce specialized reporting, The Climate Watch is expanding cross-border collaboration and investing in environmental journalism.
Founded in 2022 by award-winning Bangladeshi environmental journalist Shamsuddin Illius, The Climate Watch has developed into a regional platform connecting approximately 100 climate and environmental journalists.
“We are striving to become a voice for South Asia in global climate negotiations. Our countries are among the most vulnerable to climate change, and it is essential that we tell our own stories rather than rely solely on others to tell them for us,” Executive Editor Md Ibrahim Khalilullah said.
At COP31, its journalists will examine climate finance, adaptation, loss and damage, energy transition, biodiversity, displacement and climate justice, linking diplomatic negotiations to the everyday experiences of vulnerable communities.
The publication is also exploring collaborations with Shakti Foundation, Young Power in Social Action (YPSA) and Change Initiative to strengthen its coverage.
The Climate Watch’s investigations have examined deforestation, industrial expansion, groundwater depletion and environmental governance. An investigation into forest destruction around Chittagong’s National Special Economic Zone documented biodiversity losses, with its findings subsequently cited in public-interest litigation.
Its reporting has received international references from The Guardian, The Diplomat, Mongabay, The New Humanitarian and Fiji Sun, alongside academic citations involving Columbia University’s Climate School and the National University of Singapore.
Through its Birds in Climate Crisis initiative, the publication is producing 100 short documentaries on threatened birds, habitat destruction and changing ecosystems.
The outlet also contributed to Dark Side of the Boom, an Earth Journalism Network-coordinated investigation involving 14 newsrooms across 11 countries that examined the environmental consequences of digital infrastructure.
The collaboration received a 2026 Covering Climate Now Journalism Award, a Society of Publishers in Asia (SOPA) environmental reporting award and a special citation associated with the Osborn Elliott Prize.
Having covered COP28, COP29, COP30 and Bonn’s SB64 negotiations, The Climate Watch is also preparing to report on biodiversity negotiations at COP17 in Armenia.
Alongside its reporting, the organization conducts journalist training and pre-COP fellowships with the Center for Participatory Research and Development.
For the relatively young newsroom operating from climate-vulnerable Bangladesh, the COP31 deployment represents an effort to shift South Asia’s position in the global climate conversation from a region whose suffering is frequently reported by others to one increasingly telling its own stories.

item.title: Son of Myanmar’s Suu Kyi says had first call in five years
item.description:
The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi said he spoke Thursday to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years.
“Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express,” Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook.
Suu Kyi is under house arrest in the capital, Naypyidaw, according to Myanmar authorities, where she has been sequestered since being unseated in a 2021 military coup.
AFP could not immediately reach Aris -- who lives in the United Kingdom -- and it was not clear how he spoke to his mother, who won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize for efforts to bring democracy to Myanmar.
However, he posted images accompanying his Facebook post which appeared to show him standing outside the Myanmar embassy in London.
“I am deeply grateful to everyone who has stood by my mother and me. I believe your voices helped make this moment possible,” Aris wrote.
“But my mother is 81 and remains unjustly detained. One conversation is not regular family access.”
Myanmar’s military held Suu Kyi in almost total seclusion for five years following the February 2021 coup, which ended a tentative decade-long experiment with democracy.
But in recent months authorities have increasingly advertised the loosening of her detention and published photographs of her taking private meetings, as supporters have demanded “proof of life” of the octogenarian.
On Monday, authorities in Myanmar said she received a package from Britain’s King Charles III, including two books about soil and a “sealed diplomatic communication” from the monarch.
Buckingham Palace did not comment on the contents of the communication.
Myanmar authorities said Suu Kyi was moved from a prison in Naypyidaw to house arrest in April, and in August they published images of her meeting the nation’s Red Cross representative.
After ruling Myanmar as military chief for five years, Min Aung Hlaing -- who ousted Suu Kyi in the 2021 coup -- was earlier this year installed as civilian president.
Analysts describe the election putting him in elected office as a charade, and say he may be loosening restrictions on Suu Kyi in a bid to court international legitimacy.

item.title: Matthew McConaughey sparks 2028 presidential speculation with call for independent candidates
item.description:
Oscar-winning actor Matthew McConaughey has reignited speculation about a possible run for the US presidency in 2028 after releasing a six-minute video urging voters to give independent candidates a greater role in American politics.
Released on October 18, ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, the video encourages voters to take independent candidates seriously rather than dismiss them as protest candidates or spoilers. McConaughey, however, did not announce any plans to run for office or endorse a candidate or political party.
“Independent does not mean you’re middle of the road. Independent is the original road,” he said, presenting political independence as an alternative to the traditional Republican-Democratic divide.
According to The Telegraph, McConaughey also argued that independently elected representatives could encourage compromise in a closely divided Congress and hold both major parties accountable. He urged voters to examine candidates’ positions and determine whether their views aligned with their own beliefs.
The video has prompted renewed discussion about the actor’s political ambitions, although McConaughey has neither confirmed nor ruled out a presidential bid.
His potential entry into politics has been a subject of speculation for several years. In 2021, he considered running for governor of Texas but ultimately decided against entering the race. In July 2024, he described himself as being on a “learning tour” while exploring the possibility of public office. He later said he would not pursue a political campaign at that time.
McConaughey’s latest remarks have also attracted criticism from commentators and social media users who questioned whether independent candidates could split the vote and influence closely contested elections.
The discussion comes amid growing identification with political independence in the United States. According to Gallup, 45% of Americans identified as political independents in 2025, a record high at the time.
For now, McConaughey’s video has renewed questions about his political future, but the actor has yet to announce any plans to enter the 2028 presidential race.

item.title: Gazipur’s ‘Ulka cinema hall’ to shut down in November
item.description:
Ulka, a long-running single-screen cinema hall at Gazipur Chowrasta, is set to close permanently in November as falling attendance, mounting losses and rising operating costs make it increasingly difficult to keep the business afloat.
Mohammad Rafiq Uddin, managing director of the cinema hall, confirmed the decision, saying ticket sales from current releases are no longer sufficient to cover even electricity bills.
“The hall is struggling to survive. We are incurring losses continuously. The films currently screening cannot even cover the electricity bill,” he said.
Rafiq Uddin said films with compelling stories and established stars continue to attract audiences. However, relying on releases concentrated around the two Eid festivals is not enough to sustain a cinema hall throughout the year.
He pointed to the audience response to films starring Shakib Khan, suggesting that more releases featuring the actor outside the Eid seasons could help single-screen cinemas remain viable.
Unusually high electricity bills have added to the financial strain, according to Rafiq Uddin. With operating expenses becoming increasingly difficult to manage, the owners have decided to shut down rather than continue accumulating losses.
Audience numbers have also declined sharply, hall authorities said. Some screenings attract only a handful of moviegoers, leaving ticket revenue insufficient to cover staff salaries and routine operating expenses.
The planned closure comes as Kamruzzaman’s Sneher Bondhon is screening at the venue. Starring Joy Chowdhury and Mou Khan, the film was released in 14 cinemas on October 16.
Its promotional campaign included appearances on an open-roof bus in Dhaka. However, reports from the exhibition circuit indicate that the film has struggled to attract audiences.
The closure will further narrow cinema-going options in Gazipur, an industrial district with a large working population. Local industry sources said four cinemas were operating in the district around a year to 18 months ago.
Once Ulka closes, only Barsha and Jhumur cinemas are expected to remain open in the district. Both venues are reportedly facing financial difficulties, raising further concerns about the future of single-screen cinema in the area.
Ulka’s shutdown highlights the challenges facing traditional cinema halls in Bangladesh, where declining attendance and rising operating costs continue to put pressure on venues that have long provided relatively affordable big-screen entertainment.

item.title: Chiranjit Biswas wins ‘Best Male Actor’ at Tasveer Film Festival
item.description:
