Cantonment board services added to MyGov platform
item.description:
Citizen services provided by all cantonment boards have been brought under the MyGov platform through an initiative of the Directorate of Military Lands and Cantonments to establish a technology-driven, transparent and citizen-friendly service system.
The initiative was implemented under the overall supervision of the Cabinet Division, with support from the Aspire to Innovate (a2i) Program and the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Division.
Under the previous system, service recipients had to visit cantonment board offices in person to obtain services. Applications, document submissions, fee payments and certificate collection were handled manually, often requiring multiple visits and resulting in additional expenses, time and inconvenience.
To reduce travel, time, expenses and inconvenience for citizens, a pilot project was initially launched by incorporating 2 citizen services of the Dhaka Cantonment Board into the MyGov platform. Following the successful pilot, steps were taken to digitize services at the remaining 14 cantonment boards.
As part of the process, 3 service analysis workshops were held in March 2026, with officials and employees from the 14 cantonment boards participating. A total of 63 types of citizen services were reviewed and analyzed, and 19 basic services were identified for digitization. Subsequently, 185 online application forms were developed for these services across different cantonment boards.
In June and July 2026, 7 region-based validation workshops were held to verify and finalize the online application forms, service fees, service workflows and templates.
In August and September, 140 officials and employees, including Cantonment Executive Officers from all cantonment boards, received practical training. This completed the necessary preparations for managing services and conducting operations through the digital platform.
Currently, 185 online application forms covering 19 basic services are publicly available on the MyGov platform. Citizens can apply online from home, pay applicable service fees and receive certificates or services containing QR codes.
They can also monitor the progress of their applications online and provide feedback on the services.
Cantonment boards can receive, verify, investigate, process and dispose of applications online through the same platform. This is expected to accelerate administrative activities, reduce paperwork and strengthen transparency and accountability in service management.
As part of the current government's priorities for simplifying services and digital transformation, the inclusion of cantonment board citizen services on the MyGov platform has opened a new avenue for integrated, technology-driven service management.

item.title: PM urges officials to keep Dhaka clean for their own children
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday urged city corporation officials and employees to work sincerely to make the capital clean, healthy and liveable, at least for the sake of their own children, saying waste and poor sanitation are among Dhaka’s biggest problems.
“Forget about everyone else. Let us build a healthy environment and a healthy city for our own children. Let us all work together towards that goal,” he said.
The prime minister made the call while exchanging views with officials and employees during a visit to Dhaka South City Corporation’s (DSCC) Nagar Bhaban headquarters, said the PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
Emphasizing the need to keep the city clean for the sake of children's future, Tarique said no parent would want their children to grow up in a dirty, germ-ridden and unhealthy environment.
Children do not stay only around their homes; they also go to schools, colleges, playgrounds and other parts of the city, he said, adding that efforts to keep Dhaka clean must extend beyond individual neighborhoods.
“Your children will not stay only in your neighborhood. They will move around the whole of Dhaka. So, let us all try together. If we make an effort, we can do it,” Tarique said.
About waste and poor cleanliness issues in the capital, he said the problems could not be solved in a day or even in seven days, but sincere and sustained efforts by everyone could gradually improve the situation.
Addressing city corporation officials and employees, the prime minister said they are directly or indirectly involved in resolving the problem.
“It may take time, but if you keep trying, change will come. You must have that confidence. The most important thing is the willingness to act,” he said.
Tarique also urged officials to take greater responsibility for identifying and resolving problems, saying he regularly looked for problems wherever he went and contacted the relevant people to address them.
“If you also observe problems in this way and take steps to solve them, change is certainly possible,” he said.
Citing London as an example, the prime minister said many parts of the British capital were also littered during the 1960s and 1970s. Still, sustained efforts and public awareness gradually improved the situation.
Many people who visited clean and well-maintained cities abroad might have wished Dhaka could be like them, he said, adding that regret alone would not bring change unless people also fulfilled their responsibilities.
Referring to a recent conversation with a senior official of a South Korean company that has been doing business in Bangladesh for a long time, Tarique said the official told him that Dhaka’s cleanliness improved somewhat compared with the past.
“He did not say there has been a big change. He said it has improved somewhat. That means change is possible. If we all work together, we can do even better,” the Prime Minister said.
He also said he regularly monitor the condition of roads and waste management across the city.
Some road dividers are being rebuilt, while condition at some waste transfer stations has improved to a certain extent, he said, stressing the need to continue such initiatives.
Tarique urged officials and employees to practice self-criticism alongside criticism of others.
“You may criticize me, but you must also examine yourselves. Think about how properly you are performing your duties and how much effort you are making,” he said.
Earlier, the prime minister visited the emergency operations centre at Nagar Bhaban, where he reviewed websites displaying weather information, earthquake updates from the United States Geological Survey (USGS), wind speed, flood forecasts and air quality.
He also enquired about how the information was monitored and how officials tracked emergency situations.
Tarique monitored the city's cleanliness activities through a Facebook Live broadcast and watched a video on the development and various activities of Dhaka South City Corporation.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, DSCC Administrator Abdus Salam, Dhaka North City Corporation Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan Milton, and Local Government Division Senior Secretary Shahidul Hasan were present.

item.title: Govt trains aspiring entrepreneurs to improve agro-processing skills
item.description:
The government is providing training to help young people become entrepreneurs by improving their agricultural product processing, business management skills and market access.
The initiative is being implemented in 208 upazilas across all 64 districts under a project of the Department of Agricultural Marketing (DAM) under the Ministry of Agriculture. So far, 6,875 people have received training, while the project aims to train around 7,000 more entrepreneurs this year.
The initiative is being implemented under the Programme on Agricultural and Rural Transformation for Nutrition, Entrepreneurship and Resilience in Bangladesh (PARTNER). Its objectives include creating entrepreneurs in various agriculture-based sectors, adding value to agricultural products, and expanding opportunities for processing and exports.
The project aims to ensure that women account for 60% of the entrepreneurs developed under the initiative, while men will make up the remaining 40%.
Project officials said training is being provided to develop entrepreneurs in various sectors, including agriculture, seeds, nurseries, mushrooms, vermicompost, jute products and dairy products. Alongside technical training, the initiative focuses on strengthening business skills, management knowledge and market linkages.
Dr Muhammad Abdullah Al Faruk, agency program director of the PARTNER-DAM component of the Department of Agricultural Marketing, said the initiative was underway in 208 upazilas across all 64 districts.
He said the training was designed to improve entrepreneurs' business management skills and connect them with markets.
After completing the training, entrepreneurs are also receiving incubation support, he said. Incubation support organisations are working to identify the challenges entrepreneurs face in running their businesses and help them find solutions.
The project also plans to provide financial assistance to trained entrepreneurs to purchase agricultural product processing equipment. Under the proposed arrangement, the project will subsidise 70% of the equipment costs, while entrepreneurs will bear the remaining 30%.
The support is expected to create opportunities for small entrepreneurs to launch and expand agricultural product processing businesses.
Another key objective of the project is to improve coordination among stakeholders involved in agricultural marketing. To this end, 767 Market Actors Business Schools have been established in different agricultural production areas under the Department of Agricultural Marketing. Of these, 227 focus on potatoes. The project plans to establish another 335 schools this year.
Dr Al Faruk said the schools were being established around the dominant agricultural products of particular areas.
The initiative brings farmers, traders, entrepreneurs, cold storage owners, transport operators and other market stakeholders under a common platform. This is expected to make it easier to identify challenges and opportunities in the supply chains of specific agricultural products, he said.
The project is also working to improve the value chains of potatoes, mangoes, jackfruits, tomatoes and aromatic rice.
It aims to strengthen coordination among stakeholders at different stages, from production and collection to storage, processing and marketing. Initiatives are also underway to form Value Chain Promotional Bodies for the five products.
Project officials said the guidelines for these bodies had already been approved by the ministry.
Meanwhile, Agriculture, Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammed Aminur Rashid has stressed the importance of research, innovation and modern technology in increasing productivity across agriculture-based sectors.
He said research, innovation and the development of a skilled workforce were essential to advancing the agriculture, fisheries and livestock sectors. The government aims to develop skilled human resources in agriculture through training, he added.
Abul Kalam Azad, the project's coordinator, said entrepreneurs could create employment opportunities for others while becoming self-reliant themselves.
Initiatives to develop entrepreneurs could play an important role in making agriculture a modern and respected profession, he added.

item.title: UN agency slashes Gaza food aid over funding, warns needs persist
item.description:
The World Food Program said Monday it would end monthly assistance to 500,000 people in Gaza due to a funding shortfall, despite acute needs in the war-battered Palestinian territory.
With the cutbacks, 1.1 million Palestinians in Gaza -- still about half the population -- will be receiving either food or cash assistance each month from the UN agency, in reduced amounts.
The World Food Program said its efforts had mitigated the effects during a famine last year in Gaza -- a description of the situation disputed by Israel -- and warned that conditions had not improved to the point that it can take away aid.
“People are not safe. Airstrikes continue on a daily basis. People continue to be displaced,” Shaun Hughes, the WFP country director, told AFP at the agency’s office in east Jerusalem.
“Almost everybody remains without a permanent home to live in. And the humanitarian conditions are brutal,” he said.
According to the latest assessments, 1.4 million people -- or two-thirds of Gaza’s population -- are still “acutely food insecure” and need humanitarian assistance to survive, he said.
In August last year, the UN’s Integrated Food Security Phase Classification said that Gaza was suffering famine conditions. Israel, which has blockaded the territory and attacked it relentlessly since the October 7, 2023 resistance campaign on it by Hamas, described the finding as a lie.
The famine classification was lifted in December, two months after a US-brokered ceasefire was announced in Gaza. Israel has kept striking Gaza since then, vowing to kill anyone involved in the October 7 resistance campaign.
Since the ceasefire, the WFP has been able to step up assistance and had been reaching between 1.5 million and 1.8 million people every month.
“This has been a lifeline. But now, rather than being able to sustain and scale up that assistance, we’re actually having to reduce it,” Hughes said.
“And that’s not because we don’t have humanitarian access to deliver food; that’s because we don’t have funding.”
In addition to reducing the number of people who receive rations, the WFP has been forced to shrink the content.
Families receiving food assistance will now get only one food parcel instead of two and a smaller bag of wheat flour, the WFP said in an operational note.
The 75,000 families who receive assistance in cash will see the amount reduced from 1,250 to 750 shekels ($400 to $240) per month.
The WFP is funded by governments as well as private donors. It has seen a sharp drop in resources, including after President Donald Trump returned to power in the United States and drastically slashed contributions to UN agencies as well as bilateral aid.
The agency says it needs about $450 million over the next six months for its operations in Gaza and the West Bank, but in 2026 it has only received about half the usual financing for the Palestinian territories.
In September, the agency also reduced by half the number of aid recipients in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967, from 400,000 to 200,000.
“Now is not the time in the history of Palestine and Gaza to turn away from what is happening in Gaza,” Hughes said.
The WFP says that conditions have moderately improved in Gaza but noted that needs could rise again with the onset of winter.
Israel has allowed more goods into Gaza under the terms of the Trump ceasefire but still imposes heavy restrictions, turning away shipments of anything that is seen as having potential military use -- a policy that has included blocking even prosthetic limbs, according to the United Nations.
Israel has ramped up longstanding criticism of the United Nations since the Gaza war, accusing the world body of bias and perpetuating dependency among Palestinians.

Maha Ashtami celebrated with Kumari Puja, Sandhi Puja
item.description:
Maha Ashtami, the third day of the six-day Sharadiya Durga Puja festival, is being celebrated across the country on Monday with due religious fervour and festivity.
Maha Ashtami Kalparambha and Bihit Puja were held this morning at temples across the country, including Dhakeshwari National Temple. Devotees later offered anjali (prayers) and received charanamrito (sacred water). Maha Prasad was also distributed among devotees.
Sandhi Puja was held from 7:55am to 8:43am, marking the transitional moment between Ashtami and Navami.
According to Hindu mythology, the ritual commemorates the moment when Goddess Durga assumed the form of Chamunda to slay the demon brothers Chanda and Munda.
Kumari Puja, a traditional ritual in which a young, unmarried girl is worshipped as an embodiment of Goddess Durga and the divine feminine, was held at some temples across the country.
In the capital, Kumari Puja was held at Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission Dhaka at 9:30am.
During the ritual, an unmarried pre-pubescent girl, generally aged between one and 16, is worshipped as the living embodiment of the divine feminine and Goddess Durga.
Devotees offer water, clothes, flowers, and gold and silver ornaments at the feet of the Kumari as part of the special ritual.
Puja mandaps across the country have been bustling with devotees and visitors since last Friday, when the six-day festival began with the ceremonial invocation of Goddess Durga on Maha Shashthi.
Vibrant decorations, traditional dhak beats, the ringing of kashor and ghonta, conch-shell blasts and ululation have added to the festive atmosphere.
Devotees have been visiting puja pandals across the country to offer prayers and enjoy the celebrations.
A total of 33,851 puja mandaps have been set up across the country this year, including 258 in the capital, according to the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad. The number has increased by nearly 1,500 compared to last year.
The Gulshan-Banani Puja Foundation is hosting one of the most elaborate celebrations at Kamal Ataturk Park in Banani. Makeshift pandals at Kalabagan ground and Khamarbari have also emerged as major attractions for visitors in the capital, with large structures and eye-catching lighting displays drawing crowds.
Maha Navami will be celebrated tomorrow with religious fervour and enthusiasm. Devotees will gather at temples and mandaps to offer anjali, while major concluding worship rituals and the offering of bhog will mark the day.
Bijaya Dashami will be celebrated on Wednesday, marking the farewell to Goddess Durga. Devotees will take the idols in processions to designated rivers, ponds and other water bodies for immersion, known as Bisarjan.
In the capital, a large number of Durga Puja celebrations are being held in the old parts of the city, including Tantibazar and Shakharibazar.
Ramna Kali Mandir, Siddheshwari Kali Mandir, Dhaka University's Jagannath Hall and Uttara Sarbajanin Mandir are also witnessing large numbers of visitors every day during the festival.

NCC Bank launches ‘China Desk’ to strengthen banking services for Chinese businesses
item.description:
With the aim of providing integrated banking services to Chinese business enterprises and investors operating in Bangladesh, NCC Bank PLC has launched a specialized China Desk named ‘NCC China Connect’.
The main objective of this initiative is to accelerate bilateral trade, investment and business growth between Bangladesh and China.
The China Desk was inaugurated on Wednesday, October 14, at the ‘China National Day Celebration 2026’ held at the Grand Ballroom of Radisson Blu Hotel, Dhaka, organized by the Bangladesh China Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCCI) in collaboration with NCC Bank.
The event was held on the occasion of the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China.
The chief guest at the event was State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, MP.
Special guest was Liu Yuyin, Chargé d’Affaires of the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Bangladesh.
Members of BCCCI, chairman of NCC Bank Mohammed Nurun Newaz Salim, vice-chairman Abdus Salam, director & past chairman Amjadul Ferdous Chowdhury, director & chairman of the executive committee Khairul Alam Chaklader, director Md Moinuddin, director Mohammed Sazzad Un Newaz, director & past vice-chairman Tanzina Ali, directors Syed Asif Nizamuddin, Shamima Newaz, Morshedul Alam Chaklader, Nahid Banu, independent director Meer Sajed-Ul-Basher, and independent director & chairman of the audit committee Md Amirul Islam.
Managing director M Shamsul Arefin, additional managing director M Khurshed Alam, Md Zakir Anam & Mohammed Jamal Uddin Mazumder, deputy managing directors Mohammed Mizanur Rahman & Md Habibur Rahman along with senior officials of the bank and leaders of Chinese businesses in Bangladesh also attended.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, MP, highlighted the importance of Bangladesh-China relations in expanding trade, investment and economic cooperation.
She expressed hope that initiatives such as NCC Bank’s China Desk would facilitate business activities between the two countries and further strengthen bilateral economic relations.
Special guest Liu Yuyin welcomed the initiative to launch a specialized banking platform for Chinese business enterprises in Bangladesh. He hoped that this Desk would play a role in expanding bilateral trade and investment, increasing business connectivity and further strengthening the economic partnership between Bangladesh and China.
NCC Bank chairman Mohammad Nurun Newaz Salim said that the launch of the China Desk reflected the bank’s commitment to supporting Chinese business enterprises and expanding bilateral trade and investment between Bangladesh and China.
NCC Bank managing director M Shamsul Arefin said: “China is Bangladesh’s largest trading partner and one of the most important sources of investment. Through ‘NCC China Connect’, we want to provide integrated and specialized banking services to Chinese business enterprises, which will accelerate trade, investment and sustainable growth between the two countries. Operated under our Multinational Corporate Banking Division, this Desk will serve as a central point of contact for Chinese entrepreneurs. Through it, along with support in Mandarin, various services will be provided, including trade finance, working capital, project financing, foreign exchange transactions, bank guarantees, cash management and digital banking. Using correspondent banking relationships with 30 banks in China and a network of nearly 400 correspondent banks worldwide, we are committed to facilitating and expediting cross-border foreign trade transaction settlement with China. In addition, we are also working to create opportunities for Chinese trade transactions settlement in the Chinese currency Renminbi (RMB).”

item.title: Police ‘lost control’ during French protests, says interior minister
item.description:
French police “lost control” during nationwide protests marred by violence over the weekend, the interior minister admitted Monday, with President Emmanuel Macron calling for a security review.
Macron also refused Interior Minister Laurent Nunez’s resignation even as he acknowledged security and intelligence failures in the government response.
Saturday’s demonstrations saw some half a million people turn out across France to protest the cost of living, but morphed into some of the worst violence to rock the country in years, with town halls and shops looted and set ablaze.
More than 2,500 people were arrested, while almost 1,000 members of the security forces were injured. Injuries were also reported among protesters, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade.
“On Saturday, in some major cities, you couldn’t look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and tell them we hadn’t lost control,” Nunez said.
Nunez acknowledged a “lack of anticipation” in the deployment of security forces on Saturday, whose numbers were insufficient to deal with the large crowds of rioters and looters on the fringes of the demonstrations.
He estimated that some 60,000 law enforcement personnel had been deployed across the country that day.
“Given the damage that has been caused, it was only right that I should hand in my resignation,” Nunez said.
The presidency said in a statement that Macron had rejected the resignation, however, citing “the necessity for continued leadership of law enforcement.”
Instead, Macron ordered Nunez to “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over the failures in planning and intelligence that led to the violence.”
To end the “barricades and looting, he also requested that the interior minister promptly implement new operational methods for security forces to use on the ground in combating rioters,” the statement added.
Looting continued on Sunday, with Paris Mayor Emmanuel Gregoire saying Monday that around 30 shops had been targeted in the capital the previous day, describing the scenes as “unbearable.”
Nunez said some 350 people had been arrested in Paris on Sunday and overnight.
Nationwide, more than 2,330 people were taken into police custody over the weekend, 70 percent of whom were adults, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said Monday.
More than 2,000 shops were expected to have been affected by the weekend’s violence across France, with damage running into “hundreds of millions of euros,” according to chamber of commerce president Alain Di Crescenzo.
In an address to the nation Sunday evening, Macron slammed the “unbridled” violence and said local authorities would be able to ban -- “if necessary” -- certain rallies in coming days.
But he stopped short of announcing drastic measures, such as a state of emergency or curfew.
Saturday’s protests followed four weeks of high school student protests that at times also turned violent.

Dhaka ranks 3rd among world's most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked third among the world's most polluted cities on Monday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 171 at 9:10am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 251, while Mumbai in India ranked second with a score of 186, followed by Delhi in India fourth place with an AQI score of 169.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

Bangladesh overpower Nepal in IHF Nations Trophy opener
item.description:
Bangladesh made a winning start to the Begum Khaleda Zia IHF Nations Trophy 2026 Asia Zone-2 (Women's Senior) with a commanding 33–20 victory over Nepal at the Shaheed Captain M Mansur Ali National Handball Stadium in Dhaka on Sunday.
Alpana Akter led the hosts' charge with seven goals to earn the Player of the Match award as Bangladesh dominated their opening fixture on home soil.
The hosts went into the halftime break with a 13–9 lead before Spanish coach Ana Alonso's side stepped up their performance in the second half to secure a comfortable 13-goal victory.
Misti Khatun and Shyamoli Ming contributed six goals apiece, while captain Ismetara Nishi scored five and Sayma Jannat Sima added four. Masuda Akter netted twice, with Purnima Rani, Anuradha Pahan and Tasnia Rahman Arsha scoring one each.
Bangladesh also had to overcome an early setback when Sakiba Jannat received a straight red card. However, the hosts maintained their composure and continued to control the match despite being reduced to a player.
The victory was particularly satisfying for Alpana, who said the memory of Bangladesh's defeat to Nepal at the 2019 South Asian Games had remained with her.
“Honestly, I feel wonderful,” Alpana said after receiving the Player of the Match award. “We lost to Nepal back in 2019, and that frustration had stayed with me. I told myself that we were going to win. By the grace of the Almighty, that is exactly what happened; we pulled off the victory.”
Alpana said she encouraged her teammates to remain positive after Sakiba's dismissal.
“When Sakiba got the red card, our morale didn't break. I rallied everyone and said—no, even though she was sent off, we will avenge it by winning this match,” she said.
The match was Bangladesh's first international fixture under new head coach Alonso. Alpana believes the team's defensive organisation has improved under the Spanish coach.
“Our defense has improved significantly compared to before. Previously, our defensive line wasn't quite up to the mark. Now we are performing well on both ends—in defense and attack,” she said.
Bangladesh will face India in their second match as they continue their bid to reach the final of the four-team tournament.
Alpana expressed confidence ahead of the crucial encounter, saying the team would look to build on its opening performance.
“I thoroughly enjoyed this match; we all played exceptionally well. Tomorrow we face India, and we will definitely give our very best there too, Inshallah,” she said.

item.title: Nahida named Bangladesh Women's T20 captain
item.description:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has appointed left-arm spinner Nahida Akter as the captain of the Bangladesh women's T20 team for a one-year term.
The 26-year-old replaced Nigar Sultana Joty, who recently stepped down from the role, citing the reason to focus on her batting.
Nahida, Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker in women's T20 internationals, has established herself as one of the best spinners in the format.
Since making her international debut in 2015, Nahida has played 113 T20 internationals for Bangladesh, claiming 132 wickets. Her tally places her fifth among bowlers from ICC Full Member countries in the format.
Joty, however, congratulated her successor through a post on her official facebook page.
"Heartiest congratulations to Nahida, the new captain of the T20 team. Wishing her all the best in this new role. I believe her skills and leadership will play an important part in taking the team forward," Joty wrote.
She also expressed her belief that, despite the change in leadership, the team's passion and ambition for Bangladesh cricket would remain unchanged.
"Our roles in the team may have changed, but our passion for the red-and-green flag remains the same, as does our goal of taking Bangladesh cricket to greater heights," she added.
During Joty's tenure, Bangladesh won 32 of the 82 T20 matches.
The BCB has also appointed 24-year-old batter Sobhana Mostary as vice-captain of the women's T20 side.
Sobhana has featured in 72 T20 internationals since making her debut in 2019. She has also joined an exclusive group of Bangladeshi batters to score more than 1,000 runs in the format, becoming only the third player from the country to reach the milestone after Nigar Sultana Joti and Fargana Hoque.
Bangladesh's next T20 assignment is the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy 2026 which is scheduled to take place from November 12 to 25.

item.title: West Indies in Dhaka for Test series against Bangladesh
item.description:
The West Indies cricket team arrived in Dhaka on Sunday to play a two-match Test series against Bangladesh.
The series which is the part of ICC World Test Championship (WTC) starts on October 28.
The visiting team made a late change to the squad as allrounder Shamar Springer replaced pacer Keemo Paul, the Cricket West Indies confirmed in a statement. Paul has withdrawn him from the series due to personal and family reasons.
The visitors will play three-day warm-up match on October 22 before the first Test at Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium. The second and final Test is scheduled to begin in Sylhet International Stadium on November 5.
The West Indies last toured for Tests in Bangladesh in 2021, eventually winning the series 2-0.
So far the two teams played 11 Test series with Bangladesh winning two in 2009 and 2018. West Indies won eight series and one series ended in a draw.
Overall of the 22 Tests between the two teams, Bangladesh won five and lost 15 while two Tests were drawn.
However, Bangladesh's recent form made them heavily favourite to win the series and take a giant leap toward the WTC final. The confidence soared further following their 1-1 draw in two-match Test series in Australia recently.
Bangladesh are currently fourth in the WTC standing while West Indies are in eighth place.
West Indies squad: Roston Chase (c), Jomel Warrican (vc), Joshua Bishop, John Campbell, Tagenarine Chanderpaul, Joshua Da Silva, Justin Greaves, Kavem Hodge, Amir Jangoo, Shamar Joseph, Brandon King, Kemar Roach, Jayden Seales, Shamar Springer and Kevin Wickham.

item.title: Davidovich Fokina beats rising star Jodar to win Shanghai Masters
item.description:
Alejandro Davidovich Fokina fought back to beat rising star Rafael Jodar in the final of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday to claim the biggest title of his career.
The gutsy world number 26 from Spain outlasted his tiring compatriot 1-6, 7-6 (7/5), 6-4.
"I don't know what to say, I don't know what I feel. Just like a huge relief," Davidovich Fokina said.
It is a first title at the prestigious 1000 level for the 27-year-old, who extended his winning streak in China to 10 matches after claiming victory at an ATP 250 tournament in Chengdu.
The 20-year-old Jodar, ranked 13 and rising fast, was ruthless to start with.
He reached over his shoulder to save a point before winning it with an overhead smash as he broke for a swift 2-0 lead.
Davidovich Fokina put pressure on his backhand, but Jodar kept calm as his opponent succumbed to a series of errors.
Jodar broke again for 5-1 before closing out the first set after just 27 minutes with an ace.
Davidovich Fokina dropped serve to hand Jodar a 3-2 lead in the second set, but finally came up with some answers in the next game, falling on his back to save a point at the net and level at 3-3.
Both men battled to hold serve in a run of intense rallies, with the duo needing to restart a point during the ninth game when a ball rolled onto the court.
Davidovich Fokina was shouting in frustration but saved two break points to go up 6-5 when Jodar returned into the net.
But the younger Spaniard would not crumble, sending down a dangerous backhand to force a tie-break.
Davidovich Fokina held his nerve in the tie-break to force a decider. He was suddenly in control, breaking Jodar's serve in the first game.
Jodar grabbed back a break but the older man led 3-2 when Jodar fired long.
Jodar needed a medical timeout for his right thigh at 4-3 down.
He buckled in pain during a must-win ninth game, keeping the match alive for a bit longer but needing a trainer for his left thigh when trailing 5-4.
Davidovich Fokina sensed victory and claimed the title on his second championship point.
"This is going to be a memory for the rest of my life," the victor said during the trophy ceremony.
He also commended his opponent.
"You are 20-years-old but man, you have a future. And you're gonna be here many times."

item.description:
A passenger arriving from Abu Dhabi was arrested at Shah Amanat International Airport in Chittagong on Sunday after 566 grams of gold, worth an estimated Tk1.2 crore, were recovered from his luggage.
The gold was concealed inside a non-stick pan, a vegetable blender and a dish rack, according to airport authorities.
The passenger, Mohammad Kamrul Islam, is a resident of Banshkhali upazila in Chittagong. A case has been filed against him with Patenga police station on charges of smuggling gold.
Mohammad Ibrahim Khalil, public relations officer of Shah Amanat International Airport, said Kamrul arrived in Chittagong on a US-Bangla Airlines flight from Abu Dhabi.
During a search at the customs hall, officials found his movements suspicious and proceeded to inspect his luggage, he said.
The search was conducted under the joint supervision of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI), the National Security Intelligence (NSI) and Customs Intelligence personnel stationed at the airport.
Four gold bars weighing a total of 466 grams were recovered from inside the non-stick pan, stainless steel vegetable blender and dish rack. A gold bangle weighing 100 grams was also found in his possession.
The airport authorities estimated the market value of the recovered gold at Tk1.2 crore.
According to a statement from the airport’s public relations department, the seized gold was handed over to airport customs. Arrangements were under way to hand Kamrul over to Patenga police.

Japan to launch historic round-trip mission to Mars moon
item.description:
Japanese scientists are readying a mission to Mars’s moons to retrieve samples that could help unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth, in what aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region.
The unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe, a collaboration with US and European space agencies as well as numerous universities and tech companies, could also help lay the groundwork for eventual human exploration.
The flagship H3 rocket carrying the MMX is set to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Center Tuesday at 4:41 am, according to the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA).
“Being able to be involved in such a grand mission is incredibly exciting,” Makoto Arita, project manager of JAXA’s H3 rocket team, told reporters two days before the launch.
The spacecraft will arrive near Mars around August next year, where it will orbit one of its moons, Phobos, before landing and collecting at least 10 grams of material from the surface during three years of operating within the Martian sphere.
A rover dubbed IDEFIX -- the French name for the comic hero Asterix’s dog -- will first conduct surface observations aimed at ensuring a safe landing.
“The sampling (from) Phobos is of course the world’s first, but it means... this is the first-round trip to the Martian system,” MMX’s project manager Yasuhiro Kawakatsu told AFP.
JAXA said the mission will also explore the possibility of using Phobos as a “natural space station” by establishing the requirements for a round trip to Mars -- something “essential for crewed Mars exploration”.
It will also observe the Red Planet’s moon Deimos, although it will not land on it, before returning to Earth.
JAXA hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, a key piece of knowledge in working out how the Solar System was born.
One theory for the origin of the Martian moons -- the “giant impact” hypothesis -- is that they formed after a celestial body collided with Mars.
The “capture” hypothesis, meanwhile, postulates that the moons are asteroids captured by Mars’s gravity.
Determining which theory is correct will help reveal “how a habitable environment for life might have arisen on the terrestrial planets”, JAXA said, referring to the four rocky worlds closest to the Sun -- Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
“MMX will shed light on the transport mechanisms that delivered water, volatiles, and organic compounds from the outer Solar System to the inner rocky planet region -- processes that may have played a key role in making these worlds habitable,” said Patrick Michel, a French astrophysicist working on IDEFIX.
“If Phobos and Deimos are indeed remnants of these early delivery systems, they may hold clues to the origins of life itself, or, to be more correct, to the transport of the materials that were key to the emergence of life on rocky planets,” he told AFP.
MMX is a collaboration with France’s National Centre for Space Studies (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR), NASA, the European Space Agency (ESA), and about 20 universities and tech companies.
The development of the spacecraft’s landing legs was particularly difficult, as gravity on Phobos is extremely weak, JAXA scientists say.
Japan’s unmanned Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM) -- the “Moon Sniper” -- tipped over after touching down on Earth’s Moon in 2024, but still transmitted data and survived several two-week lunar nights.
Japan also has experience in bringing back samples from space, including JAXA’s unmanned Hayabusa-2, which returned 5.4 grams of rock and dust collected from an asteroid several hundred million kilometres from Earth in 2020.
On the upcoming mission “we have to travel very close to Mars and return”, which means escaping the planet’s heavy gravity, Kawakatsu told reporters.
Phobos orbits about 6,000 kilometres above the Martian surface.
“Going deep into what we call the ‘gravity well’ is difficult,” Kawakatsu said.
US and Chinese space agencies have been racing to be the first to return rock samples from Mars’s surface back to Earth.
NASA’s Perseverance rover, which has been roaming the Red Planet since 2021, has already collected samples.
The mission, however, was effectively cancelled by the administration of President Donald Trump following a vote by the US Congress in January.
China, meanwhile, has announced its Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and hopes to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 -- potentially before the MMX’s return.
JAXA scientists say sand and rocks from Phobos may offer a wider variety of samples than those on the planet itself, especially if it was formed by a collision between a celestial body and Mars.

item.title: EU ‘strongly condemns’ settler attack on delegation in West Bank
item.description:
The European Union said Sunday that it “strongly condemns” an attack the previous day by a group of Israeli settlers on visiting European diplomats.
“The EU strongly condemns the latest attacks by violent settlers in the West Bank, including on European diplomats,” the foreign service said in a communique.
The communique also urged “full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians, including during the ongoing olive harvest season, as well as against journalists.
“We urge Israel to fully abide by International Humanitarian and Human Rights Law, and to cease the expansion of settlements,” the statement concluded.
Saturday saw Israeli settlers attack a convoy of European diplomats in the West Bank and beat up a visiting French mayor, witnesses said, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing “crisis” in the territory a day after an American photojournalist was injured in a brutal attack.
Violence is surging ahead of bitterly fought October 27 elections in Israel, coinciding with an olive harvest repeatedly disrupted by Israeli settlers as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeks to shore up his pro-settlement right-wing base.
On Saturday, 78-year-old Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France and kicked and hit him with iron bars.
“I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Baudoux told AFP after he and visiting EU representatives were attacked.
“The whole world needs to know what’s happening,” he said.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Israel must “urgently halt criminal violence” and arrest those responsible while his Belgian counterpart issued a similar call.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,196 as seven die in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Sunday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,196.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all seven of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,092, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the seven new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with three deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,254 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Sunday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 213,244.
During the same period, 65 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 23,122.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 189,484 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 181,756 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Bangladesh, Uzbekistan discuss FTA to boost trade, investment ties
item.description:
Bangladesh and Uzbekistan discussed a free trade agreement on Sunday to boost trade and investment between the two countries.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir received Deputy Foreign Minister of Uzbekistan Aloyev Bakhromjon Juraboyevich in Baghdad on the sidelines of the 52nd OIC Council of Foreign Ministers and discussed the issues of mutual interest.
The two sides discussed advancing bilateral cooperation in diverse sectors, including cooperation in trade and investment, air connectivity, tourism, reciprocal support in multilateral fora and enhancing business-to-business contacts.
The state minister is leading the Bangladesh delegation to the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Baghdad taking place from Saturday to Sunday.
On Saturday, he delivered his statement in the plenary session of the Council and called for a stronger, modernised and dynamic OIC to address the challenges facing the entire Muslim Ummah.
State Minister Kobir on Saturday suggested restructuring the D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation (Developing-8) and undertaking more result-oriented activities to make the organization more meaningful.
He met D-8 Secretary General Sohail Mahmood on the sidelines of the 52nd OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad and discussed issues of mutual interest.
The state minister discussed various issues under the D-8 framework, including the promotion of intra-D-8 trade and investment, contract farming and visa waivers among member states.
The D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation is an organization for economic cooperation among Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Malaysia, Nigeria, Pakistan and Türkiye. Azerbaijan joined the organization in 2025.
Meanwhile, Bangladesh and Oman on Saturday discussed ways to explore partnerships in trade and investment, skilled migration, and the possibility of institutionalising a trade framework to advance bilateral relations beyond labour market-centric relations.
The state minister received the Under Secretary of Foreign Affairs of Oman Sheikh Khalifa bin Ali Al Harthy in Baghdad on the margin of the Council of Foreign Ministers (CFM) of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
The meeting also stressed the importance of more business-to-business and people-to-people contacts to translate existing bilateral relations into a more meaningful one.
State Minister Kobir and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Iraq Mohammed Hussein on Saturday signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) in Baghdad.
The MoUs were signed on the sidelines of the Council of Foreign Ministers (CFM) of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
The MoUs provide for the mutual exemption of visa requirements for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and for the establishment of a mechanism for regular political consultations between the two countries, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
At the signing ceremony, the two Ministers exchanged warm greetings and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the friendly and cooperative relations between Bangladesh and Iraq.
They expressed confidence that these agreements would give fresh momentum to bilateral engagement and open new avenues for cooperation in the days ahead.
Major General Md Maksudul Haque, Ambassador of Bangladesh to the Republic of Iraq, was also present.

item.title: Tarique says planning, goodwill can make areas clean, green
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday said proper planning and goodwill can make any area clean, green and beautiful, citing the visible transformation of Aminbazar over the past two months as an example.
“With proper planning and goodwill, an area can beautifully be transformed for the welfare and benefit of people. This place is the biggest proof of that,” he said.
The prime minister made the remarks after inaugurating a greening and beautification program along both sides of the Dhaka-Aricha highway by planting a sapling at Aminbazar while returning to Dhaka from Savar Cantonment.
He said the area has changed significantly over the past two months, creating a better environment for people living within around four kilometres of the site and making it easier for them to breathe cleaner air.
Tarique Rahman thanked Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khanom and the officials and employees of the Local Government Ministry involved in the initiative for their efforts in transforming the area.
He urged local residents to help preserve the improved environment, saying the government has developed the area, but maintaining its beauty is now also the responsibility of the people living nearby.
“Local people must take responsibility for preserving the environmental improvements. With public cooperation alongside government initiatives, pollution and waste management problems can be gradually addressed,” the prime minister said.
He asked the DC to expand the greening program to other areas under Dhaka district near Aminbazar.
Tarique Rahman also suggested discussing with owners of mills and factories along the highway the possibility of assigning them responsibility for maintaining specific stretches.
The authorities concerned should also develop plans, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, to improve and beautify areas where waste still accumulates, he said.
The prime minister called on local lawmakers to cooperate with the district administration, expressing hope that coordinated efforts by public representatives and officials will gradually resolve waste management and environmental problems.
“Everyone must work together so that people can breathe fresh air and enjoy the beauty of nature,” he said.
Tarique Rahman said the Dhaka DC has set an example for the administration in other districts through the environmental improvement and beautification work at Aminbazar.
He expressed hope that DCs of other districts will take effective steps to transform similar areas into clean, green and attractive places.
BNP Standing Committee member and local MP Amanullah Aman, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, and State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salauddin Tuku were present.
Earlier in the day, the prime minister attended a ceremony at Savar Cantonment to present National Standard to several battalions and regiments of the Bangladesh Army.

item.title: DB: Ishraque’s display of arms during anti-drug drive to be investigated
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) will take necessary action after reviewing the viral video showing State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain carrying a firearm during an anti-drug drive in the capital, said Additional Police Commissioner of the Detective Branch (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam on Sunday.
“It is not the right time to comment on the incident before assessing it. The deputy commissioner concerned will review the entire matter and submit a report. If any violation of law is found in the report, the DMP will take legal action,” he said at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre.
Asked whether a minister could perform duties similar to those of police during an operation, the DB chief declined to make any comment.
Earlier, a video of the drive was posted on Ishraque Hossain’s official Facebook page on Saturday afternoon.
The video shows him getting out of a vehicle with a loudspeaker and a pistol and then chasing a group of people during an anti-drug drive near the railway line in the capital’s Gandaria area.
At one point, he was seen pointing the weapon towards some people while shouting, “Hey, stop, stop.”
Another man in plainclothes was also seen chasing people with a weapon in his hand.
In another Facebook post on Saturday evening, Ishraque pledged to continue the drives until Dhaka-6 constituency is made free of drugs.
The state minister and Dhaka-6 MP, in a statement on Sunday, said he briefly raised his licensed firearm in “self-defence” during an anti-drug drive in the capital’s Gendaria area on Saturday after receiving warnings of possible “security threats”.
Ishraque said he, along with his security personnel, got out of their vehicles and raised the weapon briefly when a group of 30 to 35 people allegedly approached their convoy aggressively near a suspected drug den.
He claimed that law enforcement agencies and his own intelligence sources had warned him of possible security risks, including the possibility of drug traders firing at them from rooftops.
“The weapon was raised for a very short time in self-defence to protect lives and property amid fears of an imminent attack,” the state minister said, adding that it was put away as soon as the potential threat had passed.

item.title: Prime accused in Satkhira mob killing case arrested
item.description:
The Special Response Battalion (SRB-6) has arrested Fazlul Haque Amini, the prime accused in the murder of Wahiduzzaman Shamim in Debhata, Satkhira, following allegations of religious defamation.
SRB-6 Commander Lt Col Nistar Ahmed confirmed the matter.
Additional Superintendent of Police Zayen Uddin Muhammad Ziad, commander of SRB-6 Satkhira CPC-1, said an SRB-6 team arrested Amini, 45, during a raid in Bishnupur area of Kaliganj around 11:00pm on Friday based on a tip-off.
Amini, son of Qari Ruhul Amin of South Parulia in Debhata, was later handed over to Debhata police for further legal action.
According to the case statement, an audio recording of a conversation between Shamim, 38, and his wife was circulated on Facebook on October 12. After allegations that the recording contained derogatory remarks about religion, locals became agitated and attacked Shamim’s house.
The following afternoon, Shamim was allegedly dragged out of a rural doctor’s chamber at a local market and beaten while receiving treatment.
Police rescued him and admitted him to Debhata Upazila Health Complex. Later that night, around 8:30pm, a group allegedly led by Fazlul Haque Amini attacked the hospital, took Shamim away and assaulted him again.
Shamim died while being taken to Satkhira Medical College Hospital.
His elder brother Abdul Jalil later filed a murder case with Debhata Police Station, naming 10 people and accusing 200–250 unidentified individuals. Amini was named the prime accused.

item.title: Ex air force chief Sheikh Abdul Hannan arrested in Qatar
item.description:
Former Bangladesh Air Force chief Air Chief Marshal Sheikh Abdul Hannan has reportedly been arrested in Qatar in connection with corruption and money laundering cases, the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) said on Sunday.
Qatari law enforcement authorities arrested him on Thursday, ACC Secretary Saidur Rahman Khan told journalists at a briefing on Sunday afternoon.
The International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) informed the ACC of the arrest by email. However, details of where and under what circumstances he was arrested, and whether steps had been taken to bring him back to Bangladesh, were not available.
In July 2025, the ACC filed 2 separate cases against Sheikh Abdul Hannan and his wife, Tahmida Begum, over allegations of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income and money laundering.
According to the case statement filed by the ACC, Sheikh Abdul Hannan acquired assets worth Tk3 crore 28 lakh 51 thousand 506 beyond his legitimate sources of income. He was also accused of suspicious transactions totaling Tk27 crore 63 lakh 66 thousand 701 through 6 bank accounts operated in his name.
Cases were filed against him under the relevant provisions of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, Money Laundering Prevention Act and Prevention of Corruption Act.
In a separate case, the ACC accused Tahmida Begum of acquiring assets worth Tk1 crore 91 lakh 90 thousand 304 beyond her known sources of income. The case statement also cited suspicious transactions of approximately Tk1 crore 18 lakh through 32 bank accounts in her name.
Tahmida Begum was named the prime accused in that case, while Sheikh Abdul Hannan was also accused of assisting his wife in acquiring illegal assets.
Earlier, courts issued several orders concerning the assets and bank accounts of Sheikh Abdul Hannan and his family members in connection with the corruption allegations.
Most recently, on September 20, a court ordered the seizure of 34 decimals of land registered in his name following an application by the ACC.
Following his reported arrest in Qatar, it remains unclear what steps the relevant authorities will take to bring him back to Bangladesh.

AG: Initiative taken to expedite hearings in Abrar, 2 other murder cases
item.description:
Attorney General Ruhul Quddus Kazal on Sunday said a special initiative is being taken to expedite hearings in three high-profile murder cases —the Narayanganj seven-murder case, retired Major Sinha Md Rashed Khan and Buet student Abrar Fahad murder cases.
The three important cases have been awaiting hearings in the Appellate Division for a long time, he said.
He said arrangements would be made for speedy hearings once court proceedings resume after the vacation.
The trials and subsequent High Court proceedings in all three cases have been completed.
Following hearings on appeals and death references, the High Court upheld death sentences and other punishments against the accused.
On April 27, 2014, seven people, including Narayanganj City Corporation councillor Nazrul Islam and lawyer Chandan Sarker, were abducted from Narayanganj court area. They were later murdered and their bodies dumped in the Shitalakkhya River.
The incident sparked widespread outrage across the country .
Following the trial court's verdict, on August 22, 2017, the High Court upheld the death sentences of 15 of the 26 convicts sentenced to death.
Retired Major Sinha Md Rashed Khan was shot dead by police at Shamlapur checkpost in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, on the night of July 31, 2020.
Following the trial court's verdict, the High Court delivered its judgment on June 2, 2025, upholding the death sentences of Pradeep Kumar Das, the then officer-in-charge of Teknaf Police Station, and Liaqat Ali, the then inspector of Baharchhara Police Investigation Centre.
The case is now awaiting a hearing in the Appellate Division.
On the night of October 6, 2019, a group of leaders and activists of Bangladesh Chhatra League beat Abrar Fahad, a second-year student of the electrical and electronics engineering (EEE) department, to death at Sher-e-Bangla Hall of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology ( Buet ).
Following hearings on appeals and death references against the trial court's verdict, the High Court delivered its judgment on March 16, 2025, upholding the death sentences of 20 convicts and life imprisonment for five others.

No DNA lab in Cox’s Bazar may delay identification of 10 fire victims
item.description:
Identifying the 10 tourists killed in a fire at Tuptup Resto & Resort in Cox’s Bazar could take up to two weeks as authorities must send DNA samples to Dhaka for testing, with no such laboratory available in the district.
The bodies are being kept at the morgue of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital pending confirmation of their identities through DNA tests at the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) forensic DNA laboratory in Dhaka.
Meanwhile, a case was filed at Ukhiya police station on Saturday night against the resort owners in connection with the fire.
A 5-member investigation committee formed by the Cox’s Bazar district administration, led by Additional District Magistrate Tasnim Jahan, visited the scene on Sunday morning.
According to sources at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital, authorities have initiated DNA testing to establish the identities of those killed in the fire at the resort. However, the absence of a DNA laboratory and the necessary equipment in Cox’s Bazar has left them dependent on the CID’s forensic DNA laboratory in Dhaka.
As most of the bodies were severely burned, their identities could not be confirmed immediately. Blood samples or buccal swabs collected from the victims’ relatives will be sent to Dhaka for comparison with samples taken from the bodies.
The bodies will be handed over to the families once the test results are available.
Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital Resident Medical Officer Dr Subuktogin Mahmud Sohel said it could take several days to send the samples to Dhaka and receive the reports. The bodies will remain preserved at the hospital morgue until their identities are confirmed.
Dr Sohel said DNA testing was the most reliable scientific method for identifying burned or disfigured bodies. He added that the CID forensic laboratory in Dhaka was the country’s primary facility for advanced forensic DNA testing.
Samples from major murder cases and accidents in different districts are also sent to Dhaka for DNA testing, he said. However, he stressed the need to establish a DNA laboratory in a major district city such as Cox’s Bazar.
Relatives of the victims have been waiting outside the morgue at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital since Sunday morning. This reporter spoke to 2 of them.
A relative named Samushuddha said 4 bodies, including that of a child, had been sent to the hospital morgue. He said he had identified the child by a bracelet on the child’s hand, while the identities of the others would be established through DNA testing.
He broke down in tears while recalling memories of the deceased.
Another relative, Ripon, said samples had been collected from 2 locations for DNA testing: the CID office in Dhaka and the bodies kept at the Cox’s Bazar morgue. Comparing the samples would allow the families to take the bodies home, he said.
Both relatives called for the DNA tests to be completed as quickly as possible so the bodies could be handed over to their families. They also demanded the establishment of a modern DNA testing laboratory in the Chittagong division or Cox’s Bazar to reduce delays in investigating major accidents and crimes.
Local residents said major accidents, fires, maritime incidents and the recovery of unidentified bodies frequently occurred in Cox’s Bazar, a major tourism destination. They said local forensic DNA testing facilities could speed up investigations, reduce difficulties and help families receive the bodies of their loved ones sooner.
The case filed at Ukhiya police station on Saturday night names the resort owners and others in connection with the fire. Those named include resort owner Tanvir Ahmad, also known as Tanvir Sultan Mia; his business partner, Niaz Morshed; resort manager Mohammad Sumon; and 1 other person.
The 5-member investigation committee formed by the Cox’s Bazar district administration, led by Additional District Magistrate Tasnim Jahan, visited the scene on Sunday morning.

Real-time price information empowers vegetable farmers
item.description:
Thanks to mobile phones, rural vegetable growers now know the price of their produce in city markets. Farmers and small traders at the northern trading hub of Mohasthan, Bogra, say that they now come to the market with a realistic idea of prices.
Information about the prices of commodities flows freely thanks to mobile phones. Producers say this has enhanced their bargaining power though the prices ultimately depend on supply and demand.
Studies cited in development literature suggest that mobile connectivity significantly reduces the cost of searching for information. Vegetable growers now often use voice calls and SMS services to contact buyers before harvesting.
Md Aminul Islam (36), a farmer of Rahmotbala village in Bogra Sadar upazila, has grown radish, gourd, pumpkin and yard-long bean on one acre of land. On 2 October, he brought radish to Mohasthan vegetable market. "I knew the price of each maund (40 kilograms) was about Tk 1,000 three days ago, but today it has fallen to Tk 500-600 per maund. This is because of higher supply, and because the quality of this vegetable is sometimes not good when grown in hot weather,” he explained. "Farmers cannot unite to fix the price. Farmers and traders have mobile phones, so both can get information about supply and demand.”
Rabbi Molla (25), hailing from Utholi, Shibganj, who cultivated an early variety of cauliflower on about 50 decimals of land, said they get an idea of the likely prices of vegetables before harvesting by talking to other farmers and traders. "I sold some cauliflowers from the field. I come here (to Mohasthan) hoping for a higher price. Prices go up, prices go down. When the demand for vegetables in Dhaka or other cities increases, that is when wholesalers and traders offer us better prices," he pointed out.
Reading the price situation, many paikars (traders) buy seasonal vegetables from farmers and sell them to Mohasthan-based arotdars (wholesalers) who sell commodities in bulk to their counterparts in Dhaka and other cities. One such trader, Masum Islam (27) of Bichok, Shibganj, said, "I bought bitter gourd for Tk 1,600 per maund from farmers today, expecting to sell at Tk 1,800. I am struggling to get it because we don't know the exact price in advance," he said.
Wholesalers at Mohasthan buy vegetables depending on orders from wholesalers in cities, and also depending on the supply. Cucumbers, auburgines, sponge gourds, pumpkins, yard-long beans and olive are abundant at present. "The higher the supply, the higher the profitability for us. But when there is higher demand in Dhaka, the farmers also ask higher prices. Everybody keeps track of demand and supply, via phone or Facebook. Farmers now get a share of any price-hike," said Abdul Hamid Pramanik (48) of Lahiripara, Bogra, who has been operating in the wholesale market for about a decade.
The Mohasthan trading hub supplies vegetables to different cities. About 200 traders and 70 wholesalers (owners of trading houses) operate here. Al-Mamun (40) is the owner of one such arot (trading house). Maisha Traders. He observed that the use of mobile phones by farmers and small traders has revolutionized farming, ensuring farmers a fair price. "This has increased the competition in the business. You no longer see a huge difference between the price paid at the farm and the wholesale price. Of course any price-hike affects consumers, but farmers benefit," he added.
Hefzul Bari Fakir (40), a representative of Bishal Bhandar wholesale trading house in Mirpur, Dhaka, was at Mohasthan. He said, "I get orders with the likely price from Dhaka via mobile phone. I buy vegetables from farmers and small traders and transport them to Dhaka. Farmers have access to market information, and try to sell to whoever offers them a better price. If production falls, or if there is a problem in communication, vegetable prices go up."
Vegetables are perishable and spoil quickly. Experts have estimated that 30% of the vegetables harvested spoil before reaching consumers. As farmers and traders are now able to get price information quickly, this should help them to sell their vegetables quickly. It is hoped that this will reduce spoilage.

item.title: 4 members of a family from Jessore still missing after Cox’s Bazar resort fire
item.description:
Four members of a family from Jessore have remained missing following the fire at Tuptup Resto & Resort in Ukhiya of Cox’s Bazar on Saturday.
The missing family members are Nahidur Rahman, 41, son of Matiar Rahman of Mohonpur village under Manirampur Municipality in Jashore; his wife, Afsana Matin Tanji, 36; and their two children, Ruzaina Inaya, 7, and Sunaina Ihana, 3.
Family sources said Nahidur worked at an organization called Grand Power Limited in Shyamoli, Dhaka. He used to live with his wife and children in Shewrapara, Mirpur.
Nahidur’s elder brother, Zahidur Rahman Prince, said they learned from the resort booking bill that Nahidur had reserved a room at Tuptup Resto & Resort from October 16 to 18. He made the booking on October 11 and was scheduled to check out at 1pm on Sunday.
Zahidur said Nahidur told the family that he would travel to Cox’s Bazar on Friday.
After learning about the fire on Saturday, he repeatedly called his younger brother but could not reach him or any other family member.
“We still cannot confirm whether they are alive or dead. We are extremely worried about them,” he said.
Zahidur said Additional Superintendent of Police in Cox’s Bazar, Ahidur Rahman, informed him that a person named Nahid has been reported missing.
The police official also said DNA samples are being collected to identify the bodies, and the remaining four could possibly be Nahidur’s family members, he said.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 8th globally with ‘unhealthy’ air quality
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 8th among the world's most polluted cities on Sunday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 177 at 8:50am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 239, while Delhi in India ranked second with a score of 207, followed by Singapore in Singapore third place with an AQI score of 204.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.description:
The Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has launched a special drive in the New Market area to intensify cleaning activities and clear footpaths as part of efforts to prevent dengue.
DSCC Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam led the drive after inaugurating the weekly “Cleaning Day” programme on Saturday. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inspected cleaning and mosquito-control activities in DSCC areas as part of the government’s weekly “Cleaning Day” programme aimed at preventing dengue.
During a surprise inspection on Saturday morning, the prime minister visited Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School, the Green Road Government Staff Quarters and the government residential area in Azimpur.
Speaking to students at Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School, Tarique Rahman stressed the importance of environmental protection, dengue prevention and maintaining cleanliness. He also encouraged students to plant trees to help reduce environmental pollution.
At the Green Road and Azimpur residential areas, he spoke with residents and urged them to keep their surroundings clean and remove stagnant water to prevent dengue.
He also inspected cleanliness activities along the main roads and surrounding areas and instructed officials to take necessary measures.
Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives State Minister Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Abu Abdullah Md Saleh, DSCC Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam and senior government officials accompanied the prime minister during the inspections.
The DSCC said special cleaning drives were conducted simultaneously in all 75 wards as part of the weekly “Cleaning Day” programme. City corporation cleaners and mosquito-control workers, along with local residents, took part in the campaign. Awareness rallies and microphone announcements were also organised throughout the day in different wards to encourage public participation.

item.title: Metro rail's Motijheel to Kamalapur expected to open in July next year
item.description:
The much-anticipated extension of Metro Rail's MRT Line-6 from Motijheel to Kamalapur is expected to open for commercial operations in July next year.
“The overall physical progress of the civil construction work on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension of MRT Line-6 has reached 84.85%,” Project Director of the Dhaka Mass Transit Development Project (MRT Line-6), Brigadier General (Retd) Md Abdul Wohab, told BSS here on Saturday.
He said mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) works at Kamalapur station are underway, while equipment manufactured abroad will be installed soon after being brought into the country.
According to project details, electro-mechanical works on the extension have progressed by 58%, while construction of the 1.16-kilometre viaduct on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension has been completed, and it has been handed over to Contract Package-7 (CP-07) for rail track installation.
The structural work on Kamalapur MRT Station has also been completed, while MEP and architectural works are underway and are expected to be finished by December 31, 2026.
Meanwhile, work on seven integrated electro-mechanical subsystems under CP-07 is progressing. These include electrical and track systems, signaling, automatic fare collection (AFC), platform screen doors (PSD), telecommunications, lifts and escalators.
The 21.26-kilometre MRT Line-6, extending from Uttara North to Kamalapur, is progressing towards completion. As of September 30, 2026, the physical progress of the Uttara North-Motijheel section stood at 99.67%, while civil construction work on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension had reached 84.85%.
Once the final section becomes operational, MRT Line-6 will connect Uttara North (Diabari) directly to Kamalapur Railway Station, completing the full 21.26-kilometre route.
The line will have 17 stations, including major stops at Mirpur-10, Agargaon, Farmgate and Dhaka University.
The metro rail began operating on the Uttara–Agargaon section on December 28, 2022. The Agargaon–Motijheel section opened on November 4, 2023. Since the Motijheel section opened, the metro rail has become a vital transport link for Dhaka residents, serving thousands of commuters daily.
Under the current schedule, the first trains depart from Motijheel at 7am and Uttara North at 6:40am.
On average, more than 0.4 million passengers have travelled on the metro rail since its launch, while on September 10, over 0.5 million passengers travelled on the metro, according to project information.
Revenue from ticket sales is also increasing as passenger numbers grow.
