item.title: FSCD DG: All 538 fire stations prepared for emergencies during Durga Puja
item.description:
Fire Service and Civil Defense (FSCD) has taken comprehensive measures to ensure fire safety at Durga Puja venues across the country, with all 538 fire stations ready to respond to emergencies during the festival.
Director General of Fire Service and Civil Defense Brigadier General Sultanul Afreen Junaid disclosed the preparations at a press conference held at the department’s headquarters in Dhaka on Saturday.
He said fire stations would remain on standby throughout the festival, monitoring fire safety at puja mandaps in their respective areas and maintaining round-the-clock communication with local administrations and puja committees.
During inspections, fire service personnel will assess fire risks and advise organizers on measures to address them.
They will also publicize the telephone numbers of nearby fire stations and the 102 hotlines for emergency assistance, he added.
Temporary fire stations operating in different locations will remain on high alert, while officials at divisional, district and zonal levels will stay on standby to inspect puja venues and respond to emergencies.
The director general also said the central control room and all divisional control rooms would operate round the clock. Upon receiving an emergency call, they would direct one or more nearby fire stations to respond immediately.
All divisional and district offices, along with fire stations, will coordinate continuously with local administrations and take necessary decisions and implement measures in line with their directions, he said.
At immersion sites, the department will deploy personnel and volunteers, road rescue equipment and ambulances. Lighting units will also be deployed at night where necessary.
Control rooms will be maintained at the department’s headquarters and divisional and district headquarters to ensure continuous communication with fire stations under their respective jurisdictions.
Calling for greater public awareness, Sultanul Afreen said, “Awareness is protection,” and sought the media’s cooperation in raising awareness about fire safety alongside the department’s own efforts.

item.title: Legal notice seeks probe into possible use of dengue as biological weapon
item.description:
A legal notice has been served on the government seeking a high-level scientific investigation into the unusually high dengue mortality in Bangladesh and possible genetic mutations of the virus, including an inquiry into allegations that it could be linked to a covert biological attack.
The notice also demands the establishment of an internationally accredited research laboratory to prevent and investigate biological weapons threats.
Supreme Court lawyer Md Mahmudul Hasan Mamun served the notice on Saturday in the public interest.
It was addressed to the secretaries of the ministries of defence, home affairs, health and family welfare, and foreign affairs, as well as the administrators of Dhaka North and South city corporations. A copy was also sent to the United Nations resident coordinator in Bangladesh.
The notice describes dengue as a severe public health crisis rather than a routine illness, arguing that the recurring deaths and growing number of cases warrant investigation beyond conventional mosquito-control measures.
Citing books on biological warfare and medical research, Mamun, who is also studying for a Master of Public Health degree, refers to historical accounts of plans to use disease-carrying insects in biological attacks.
The notice cites The A to Z of Nuclear, Biological, and Chemical Warfare (2019), by Benjamin C Garrett and John Hart, which discusses a Japanese military plan during World War II, codenamed “Operation PX”. According to the notice, the plan involved releasing insects carrying pathogens linked to dengue, plague, cholera and typhus along the US coast.
It also refers to Anthony Tu’s book Chemical and Biological Weapons and Terrorism (2018), which the notice says discusses the classification of dengue virus among biological agents considered for weaponisation by the US military.
Another reference is Advances in Biological and Chemical Terrorism Countermeasures (2008), edited by Ronald J Kendall and other experts. The notice cites the publication in support of its concerns about the potential misuse of disease-causing agents.
The notice argues that Bangladesh’s high population density and mosquito prevalence, alongside the reported severity of recent dengue outbreaks, warrant an urgent scientific and forensic investigation. It calls for epidemiologists, virologists and public health specialists to examine the virus’s genetic characteristics, origin and transmission mechanisms to determine whether there is evidence of deliberate or artificial modification.
However, the notice does not present evidence establishing that the dengue outbreak in Bangladesh resulted from a biological attack.
Mamun also cites Bangladesh’s obligations under international law, noting that the country is a signatory to the Biological Weapons Convention (BWC). He refers to Articles I and X of the convention, which prohibit biological weapons and address the peaceful use of biological science, as well as United Nations Security Council Resolution 1540 of 2004, which requires states to take measures against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.
The notice further invokes Articles 18(1) and 32 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, concerning the state’s responsibility to improve public health and the right to life.
It asks the authorities to arrange an expert-led genetic and forensic investigation into the dengue virus within 10 days to assess whether there is any evidence of an artificial biological attack. It also calls for the immediate establishment of a high-security laboratory for research into biological weapons prevention and comprehensive, science-based measures to control Aedes mosquitoes.
The notice warns that failure to meet the demands could lead to a public interest litigation petition before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court under Article 102 of the Constitution, seeking measures to protect public health, national security and citizens’ lives.

item.title: Russia hails Trump waiving sanctions as ‘historic’
item.description:
Russia on Saturday hailed US President Donald Trump’s move to waive new sanctions on it as “historic,” as Ukraine worries he is taking Moscow’s side in Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.
Trump signed an executive order Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions targeting Russia’s energy revenues amid a clash with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
The decision came despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine -- especially its capital, Kyiv -- in the fifth year of its offensive, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
“The Trump administration’s suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment,” Kirill Dmitriev, envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, said on social media.
The Lindsey Graham Act -- named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill -- targeted Russia’s energy and defense sectors, as well as Putin and the so-called “shadow fleet” of tankers used by Moscow to circumvent Western sanctions.
The Kremlin and Putin have not yet reacted to the move, which is a major diplomatic win for Moscow.
Dmitriev said the act would have caused “serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets.”
Trump’s waiver comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease existing sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets.
He announced the executive order Friday, shortly after Putin appeared in military uniform and said Moscow aims to capture the rest of east Ukraine.
US-led talks to end the war in Ukraine have not led to a breakthrough. Both Putin and Zelensky have frustrated Trump in the past with a lack of progress in halting the grinding war.
The move is bound to spook Ukraine’s European allies, who worry the White House is taking the Kremlin’s side.
Zelensky rallied his allies Friday on a visit to Brussels for a European Union summit, urging them to keep financing Ukraine’s fight and insisting he was standing up for his country amid the row with Trump.
Russian forces struck Ukraine’s southern city of Kherson Saturday after Trump’s announcement, killing one person and wounding 22, local officials said.
Russia has increased strikes on Kyiv in recent weeks, squeezing the city as Ukrainians brace for another winter of war.
Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defenses ahead of winter.
Russia controls large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine and Putin has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine by force.
“On the whole I see a positive trend in the operations of the troop groupings,” Putin told army leaders Friday, dressed in military attire.
“Undoubtedly, one of the main objectives remains the liberation of the Donetsk People’s Republic,” he added, using the Kremlin’s name for the eastern Donetsk region.
European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky Friday as he grappled with Trump.
“This is no time to withdraw support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia’s sanctions,” said European Council chief Antonio Costa.
“Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure.”
European concerns have been heightened by disruptions to a critical US-provided satellite system that has hampered Ukraine’s ability to counter Russia’s intense bombardments.

Dhaka's air quality remains 'unhealthy'
item.description:
The air quality in Dhaka remained unhealthy on Saturday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 166 at 9:14am.
With this score, the capital ranked ninth among the world's most polluted cities.
Iraq’s Baghdad, Singapore’s Singapore, Pakistan’s Lahore and India’s Mumbai occupied the top four spots on the list, with AQI scores of 378, 206, 201 and 192, respectively.
An AQI score between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate" with an acceptable air quality, while one between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while a score between 151 and 200 is classified as "unhealthy."
AQI readings between 201 and 300 are termed "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is considered "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Former additional secretary found dead at Officers Club
item.description:
The body of former additional secretary Md Mosharraf Hossain was recovered from a building under construction at the Officers Club in Dhaka’s Ramna area on Friday morning.
Police recovered the body around 11:45am.
Mosharraf Hossain, a member of the Officers Club, lived with his family in Banani.
According to reports, he arrived at the club around 10am with his youngest daughter. He left her near the swimming pool, beside the building under construction, and entered the structure.
About an hour later, his body was found in a bloodied condition on the ground floor near a staircase.
Sheikh Zahidul Islam, deputy commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Ramna division, said Mosharraf had poor eyesight and apparently fell from the third floor into an open space on the ground floor.
“We have completed the preliminary examination of the body,” he said.
The deputy commissioner said the family had requested that no post-mortem examination be conducted and that the body would be handed over to them.
Mosharraf’s eldest daughter lives in the United States. According to the family, his burial will take place after she arrives in Bangladesh.

item.title: Dengue: Four more die, 1,181 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Four people died of dengue, and 1,181 were hospitalized after being infected with dengue in the last 24 hours till 8am on Friday, according to a regular report of Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
With four deaths in the past 24 hours, the death toll from the disease stood at 335 this year.
Of the newly hospitalized dengue patients, 410 were in Dhaka Division, 92 in Mymensingh Division, 242 in Chittagong Division, 140 in Khulna Division, 99 in Rajshahi, 71 in Rangpur Division and 127 in Barisal Division.
According to the report, a total of 108,440 dengue patients have so far been hospitalized across the country this year.
However, in the last 24 hours, 1,179 patients recovered and were discharged from hospitals.
So far, 102,210 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the disease last year.

Four die after gas cylinder blast in Narayanganj
item.description:
All four people who suffered burn injuries in a gas cylinder blast in Kachpur, Narayanganj, have died, including a husband and wife.
The latest victim, Rony, 19, died while undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka on Friday morning.
Dr Sultan Mahmud Shikder of the institute confirmed his death.
Earlier, Rozina, 30, died on the afternoon of October 14. Her husband Sharif, 34, died early on October 15, while her brother Riaz, 22, died later that day.
Rozina suffered burns to 60% of her body, while Sharif and Riaz sustained burns to 40% each. Rony had burns covering 70% of his body.
The blast occurred around 1:30am on October 10 in a room on the second floor of a six-storey building in Sonapur, Kachpur.
Four people were severely burned in the explosion, which was reportedly caused by a gas cylinder leak.
The victims were identified as tenant Rozina, her husband Sharif, her brother Riaz and another tenant, Rony.
Hearing the blast, local residents rushed to the scene and rescued the victims before taking them to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka for treatment.

item.title: National Parliament committee proposes annual assessments to enhance education quality
item.description:
The Standing Committee on the Ministry of Education of the 13th National Parliament has recommended introducing an annual assessment system aligned with international standards to improve quality of education and move beyond artificial competition over pass rates.
At its first meeting held at the National Parliament Building on September 10, the committee proposed a series of measures to ensure transparency in education spending, tackle irregularities and corruption, investigate declining secondary-level enrolment, strengthen teacher training and expand technical education.
Chairman of the committee and Member of Parliament Md Salim Bhuiyan told Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS) at the Secretariat yesterday that the previous government had focused on numerical indicators and pass rates rather than genuine educational quality.
“Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government does not believe in this artificial competition. We want to ensure genuine quality in education in the country,” he said.
He stressed the need for annual assessments, a modern curriculum and evaluations of learning outcomes at three- or six-month intervals to bring students in line with international standards.
Further recommendations and details of the government's education roadmap will be presented at a press conference, he added.
Committee member Reza Kibria also emphasized setting specific annual benchmarks to ensure Bangladeshi students perform competitively in international assessments, particularly in mathematics and science.
Members proposed a long-term national education vision, modelled on Malaysia, to prevent frequent changes to education policies, curricula and textbooks following changes in government.
According to the meeting minutes, the government has proposed a budget of Tk57,301.68 crore for the Secondary and Higher Education Division in the 2026-27 fiscal year, 42.7% higher than the previous revised budget.
The initiatives discussed included distributing laptops to approximately 40,000 students who achieved a Golden GPA in 2026 and bringing seven million female students under a Tk4,000 crore scholarship program to promote girls’ education and reduce dropout rates.
The committee also acknowledged the transfer of outstanding dues to the bank accounts of around 70,000 retired teachers and employees through the Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) and iBAS systems.
In the initial phase, each teacher is receiving an average of Tk5 lakh.
The committee thanked Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for providing Tk2,000 crore in special assistance to address the crisis involving teachers' welfare and retirement benefits.
It recommended expediting MPO enlistment for eligible non-MPO institutions and long-serving teachers, reducing bureaucratic delays and investigating the significant decline in secondary-level enrolment.
Technical and Madrasah Education Division Secretary (routine charge) Shamsur Rahman Khan informed the meeting that technical education enrolment reached 19.16% in 2025, with a target of 30% by 2030.
Other decisions included field visits by committee members to inspect educational institutions, mandatory attendance of education board heads and National University representatives at future meetings, and faster settlement of outstanding allowances, subject to budget availability.
Educationists have welcomed the proposals, particularly the shift towards measurable learning outcomes and international standards, as potentially significant steps towards improving education quality.

item.title: Speakers: Climate-vulnerable countries must not be pushed into debt trap
item.description:
Climate-vulnerable countries must not be pushed into a new debt trap in the name of climate adaptation, speakers said at a human chain program in Mongla on Friday.
They said developed countries and corporations continue to profit from fossil fuel-dependent economies, while farmers, workers and climate-vulnerable nations bear the brunt of cyclones, droughts, river erosion and crop losses.
The speakers called for a just transition to green energy, environmental protection, climate justice and public ownership of resources.
The human chain program was held at Mithekhali Bazar in Mongla, coinciding with the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, scheduled for October 12-18. The event focused on the question of whose interests the global economy serves.
Dharitri Rakkhay Amra, Pashur River Waterkeeper, Udayan Youth Sangha, and Waterkeepers Bangladesh jointly organised the program.
Nur Alam Sheikh, a central leader of DHORA and Pashur River Waterkeeper, presided over the event. Speakers included Prof Nazrul Islam, labour leader Nazmul Haque, DHORA leader Molla Al Mamun, farmer leader Asaduzzaman Tito, SM Jane Alam Babu of Udayan Youth Sangha, youth leaders Sheikh Sifatullah Shuvo and Arafat Durjoy, and Mehedi Hasan of Waterkeepers Bangladesh.
Nazmul Haque said developing countries were struggling to repay foreign loans and interest while meeting essential spending needs in education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection. High interest rates, rising energy prices and climate-related disasters were further aggravating the crisis, he said.
“If people’s fundamental rights are curtailed to repay loans, who is development for?” he asked, stressing that public needs must take precedence over lenders’ conditions.
In his address, Nur Alam Sheikh said communities affected by climate change should receive fair compensation, not loans, for the losses and damage they suffer. “We must build a world for people, not for profit,” he said, calling for adequate climate financing and investment in renewable energy.
He also urged the government to ensure that food was treated as a fundamental human right rather than a source of corporate profit, promote environmentally friendly agriculture and ensure a just transition to green energy.
“Financing renewable energy is financing climate action,” he said, calling for an immediate shift to renewable energy.

item.title: Durga Puja begins in Gopalganj, Sunamganj with festive fervour
item.description:
The five-day Sharadiya Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of the Hindu community, began in Gopalganj on Friday with Maha Shashthi rituals, including the invocation and ceremonial welcome of the goddess.
According to the traditional calendar, this year's celebrations will continue for six days, ending on Wednesday, with Bijoya Dashami and the immersion of idols.
The festivities began gathering momentum on Thursday evening, when temples and puja mandaps across the district were illuminated with colourful lights and decorated with elaborate pandals, ornate gates and eye-catching designs. The sound of drums and conch shells added to the festive atmosphere as devotees visited the mandaps to offer prayers, take photographs and celebrate.
Priests performed Shashthi rituals on Friday morning, formally welcoming Goddess Durga to the mortal world from her heavenly abode on Mount Kailash, accompanied by her four children — Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik and Ganesha.
The goddess's face will be unveiled at the mandaps on Saturday, marking Maha Saptami. Saptami rituals will continue tomorrow, followed by Ashtami on Monday, Navami on Tuesday and Dashami on Wednesday.
This year, Durga Puja is being celebrated at 1,288 mandaps across Gopalganj's five upazilas and four municipalities. Security has been strengthened at the venues to ensure peaceful celebrations.
Sanjay Sikdar, general secretary of the Gopalganj district unit of the Puja Udjapan Parishad, said devotees would bid farewell to the goddess through idol immersion on Dashami, before welcoming her again the following year.
Dipankar Chakraborty, a priest at Shahapara Temple in the town, said the goddess arrived this year riding a horse and would depart by boat. According to traditional beliefs, the two modes of transport symbolise social uncertainty and agricultural prosperity, respectively.
Durga Puja is also being celebrated at 445 mandaps across Sunamganj. The five-day festival began on Friday with Maha Shashthi and will conclude on Bijoya Dashami.
The Special Response Battalion (SRB) has stepped up surveillance on social media to prevent rumours and misinformation that could disrupt communal harmony during Durga Puja.
Its cyber team is monitoring Facebook, Instagram and other platforms around the clock, said Wing Commander Tajminur Rahman Chowdhury, commander of SRB-9 Sylhet.
He made the remarks on Friday after inspecting security arrangements at the Durgabari Puja Mandap in Sunamganj town.
He said bomb disposal teams were ready to respond to reports of suspected explosives near puja mandaps. Drone surveillance, special patrols and dog squads have been deployed, while speedboats remain on standby for remote areas. Helicopter support will be provided if necessary.
A strong security cordon has been established across the four districts under SRB-9 to maintain law and order, he added. The force will remain on duty until Bijoya Dashami, the final day of the festival.

Eighteen passenger railway coaches arrive from India
item.description:
Eighteen broad-gauge passenger railway coaches imported from India entered Bangladesh through the Darshana-Jaynagar border in Chuadanga at 3pm on Friday.
After completing customs formalities at Darshana, the coaches will be taken to Bangladesh Railway’s workshop in Saidpur for inspection before being added to the railway fleet.
The coaches began their journey from Kapurthala in India’s Punjab state on Monday, October 12. They remained at Ranaghat Station in Kolkata before departing on Friday afternoon.
After completing formalities at India’s Gede border checkpoint, the coaches entered Bangladesh through the Darshana-Jaynagar border. Officials of Bangladesh Railway’s Pakshey division subsequently took charge of the shipment.
The coaches have been painted red and green. The shipment includes 3 air-conditioned chair coaches, air-conditioned berth coaches, 4 luggage vans and 11 Shovon chair coaches.
In May 2024, the Bangladesh government signed an agreement with India’s RITES Limited under a project to purchase broad-gauge railway coaches.
The coaches were procured from RITES Limited in India. A total of 200 coaches will be collected from India in several phases and added to Bangladesh Railway’s fleet.
Robiul Islam, divisional mechanical engineer of Bangladesh Railway’s Pakshey division, said 18 broad-gauge passenger coaches had entered Bangladesh from India on Friday.
He said the coaches belonged to different categories and that the government had taken the initiative to improve the quality of passenger services.

item.title: Two arrested over mob killing in Satkhira, prime accused at large
item.description:
A murder case has been filed over the lyincing of Wahiduzzaman Shamim, a man with mental health issues, in Debhata, Satkhira, following allegations of religious insult and incitement through Facebook Live and posts.
Shamim’s elder brother, Abdul Jalil, filed the case with Debhata police station on Thursday night, naming 10 people, with Fazlul Haque Ameni of Parulia named as the prime accused. Another 200-250 unidentified people have also been accused.
Police have arrested two people in connection with the case, including Moktar Hossain and Asadul Molla.
According to the case statement and family members, Shamim became involved in a domestic dispute with his wife on Monday evening and allegedly used abusive language. A local person later circulated an audio recording of the exchange on social media.
Claiming that the recording contained derogatory remarks, local resident Fazlul Haque Ameni went live on Facebook and called on the people to attack Shamim.
A mob subsequently attacked the family’s home and vandalised property.
Shamim was also assaulted near Subarnabad market, according to his elder brother, Abdul Jalil.
Following the attack, Shamim returned home and consumed poison, his family said.
He was taken to the chamber of a local physician, MA Sabur, in the Kuliya area, where he received treatment and was kept under observation.
On Tuesday, a mob entered the doctor’s chamber and attacked him again. Police intervened, rescued Shamim and took him to Sakhipur Health Complex.
However, the violence did not end there.
According to the family, another large mob entered the health facility, assaulted Shamim and dragged him outside.
Jalil alleged that Ameni led the crowd, which he estimated numbered more than 1,000 people.
The attackers allegedly slammed Shamim against a wall and beat him severely.
Police subsequently recovered him and transferred him to Satkhira Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
OC Shahin confirmed that Shamim had been attacked again after police initially rescued him.
“At 8:30pm, an agitated mob, or ‘Tawhidi Janata’, whatever one might call them, arrived and assaulted him again,” he said.
Shamim’s family described the killing as deliberate and demanded action against those responsible for mobilising the crowd.
“They incited people against him using a provocative video/audio clip, and then deliberately and systematically beat him to death,” Sagar said.
Sagar said his brother had completed his Honours and Master’s degrees in History at Jagannath University.
According to the family, Shamim developed mental health problems after being drugged by criminals during a bus journey several years ago.
He had experienced periods of mental instability for around a decade and had been receiving medical treatment.
The family said his condition had affected his personal life, including his first marriage.
Shamim leaves behind two sons, one from each marriage.
Sagar questioned why his brother had been subjected to mob violence instead of being dealt with through the legal system.
“If the law had punished him, we would have accepted it. But why should my brother be beaten to death without any trial?” he said.
The victim’s family also alleged that local Jamaat-e-Islami activists were involved in mobilising people during the initial attack.
Sagar claimed that some participants had gathered at a local Jamaat office before proceeding to the family’s home.
He alleged that local party leaders and activists were among those involved.
However, Kamrul Islam Gazi, president of the Ward 8 Jamaat-e-Islami unit in Parulia Union, denied the allegations.
He told BBC Bangla that local residents, rather than Jamaat activists, had assaulted Shamim.
“No... it was the local residents,” he said when asked whether party members were involved.
Gazi said he had heard that Shamim was beaten after being taken for treatment following his consumption of poison.
The family’s allegations against Jamaat members have not been independently established.
As of 3pm on Thursday, no murder case had been filed, according to police.
OC Shahin said police had contacted the victim’s family and were expecting them to visit the police station to lodge a complaint.
Sagar also said the family intended to file a case later in the day.
Police said the investigation was continuing and that legal action would be taken against those identified as responsible.

item.title: Two women killed in road accident in Shyamoli
item.description:
Two women were killed after being hit by a speeding vehicle while crossing the road in the capital’s Shyamoli area early Friday.
One of the victims was identified as Mukta, 40, while the identity of the other woman, estimated to be around 45, has yet to be confirmed.
Both were reportedly residents of the area.
The accident occurred beneath the overbridge near Shyamoli intersection early on Friday.
Police said a speeding vehicle struck the two women as they were crossing the road and fled the scene. One woman died on the spot.
Mohammadpur police rushed to the scene and rescued Mukta in an injured condition before taking her to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where she died while undergoing treatment.
The bodies have been kept in the hospital morgue for autopsies.
Mohammadpur police station Officer-in-Charge Abdul Halim said police had identified one of the victims but were still trying to establish the other woman’s identity.
He added that police were also working to identify the vehicle involved in the accident.
